Unit 1: Our Community • Class 4 EVS (New NEP 2020)

Chapter 1: Living Together

Family Structures, Joint & Nuclear Families, Mutual Responsibilities & Caring for Elders

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Diverse family structures in India: Joint families, nuclear families, single-parent homes, and extended family networks.
  • Sharing household chores equitably among all family members without gender stereotyping.
  • Caring for elders and differently-abled family members with patience, affection, and dignity.
  • Family traditions, cultural celebrations, and tracing family generations through family trees.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is the difference between a nuclear family and a joint family? How does sharing daily household chores help family members? Concept Explanation • Family Dynamics 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Nuclear Family vs. Joint Family:
• Nuclear Family: Consists only of parents and their children living together in a household.
• Joint Family: An extended family where grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts, and cousins all live together under one roof, sharing a common kitchen and household resources.

2. Benefits of Sharing Household Chores:
When chores like cooking, cleaning, gardening, and washing dishes are distributed among all members: (a) No single person (especially mothers) gets overburdened, (b) Children learn practical life skills and self-reliance, and (c) It builds mutual respect and deep family bonding.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear contrast between nuclear and joint family 1.5 M
Three tangible benefits of shared domestic chores 1.5 M
Q2 What is a 'family tree'? Distinguish between maternal and paternal relatives with two examples each. Observation & Field Work • Family Tree 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Family Tree:
A family tree is a graphical diagram that illustrates the relationships between different generations of a family, starting from the oldest ancestors (grandparents or great-grandparents) down to the youngest children.

2. Paternal vs. Maternal Relatives:
• Paternal Relatives (from Father's side): Paternal Grandfather (Dada ji), Paternal Grandmother (Dadi ji), Father's brother (Chacha ji / Tau ji), Father's sister (Bua ji).
• Maternal Relatives (from Mother's side): Maternal Grandfather (Nana ji), Maternal Grandmother (Nani ji), Mother's brother (Mama ji), Mother's sister (Masi ji).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate definition of a family tree across generations 1.5 M
Correct differentiation and examples of paternal and maternal relatives 1.5 M
Q3 Why do elderly family members require special care and attention? List three practical ways children can support grandparents at home. Think and Discuss • Caring for Elders 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why Elders Need Special Care:
As people grow old, their physical strength diminishes, vision and hearing weaken, joints become stiff, and they may suffer from chronic health conditions. They also feel lonely if not engaged in family conversations.

2. Ways Children Can Help:
• Physical Assistance: Fetching water, glasses, or medicines on time, and helping them walk safely without slippery obstacles.
• Emotional Companionship: Sitting with them, listening attentively to their life stories, and reading newspapers or books aloud to them.
• Digital Assistance: Helping them dial phone numbers or video call relatives on smartphones with patience and kindness.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific and emotional reasons for elder vulnerability 1.5 M
Three realistic, actionable ways children can support elders 1.5 M
Q4 What are the common reasons why families move from one place to another? How can a child adapt to a new neighbourhood? Life Skills & Values • Changing Families 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Reasons for Family Relocation:
• Job Transfers & Employment: Parents moving to new cities for work opportunities or promotions.
• Higher Education: Shifting to cities with better schools, colleges, and training centres.
• Natural Calamities: Temporary or permanent displacement due to floods, earthquakes, or droughts.

2. Adapting to a New Neighbourhood:
A child can adapt smoothly by: introducing themselves politely to neighborhood children in the park, learning local customs and language, participating in community festivals, and keeping in touch with old friends while embracing new ones.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Valid reasons for migration/relocation 1.0 M
Positive psychological strategies for adapting to a new environment 1.0 M
Q5 In what ways do family members help and support each other in daily household chores and during illness? Family Dynamics • Roles & Cooperation 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Family Support & Cooperation:
1. Sharing Chores: Parents cook meals, wash clothes, and earn a livelihood, while children help by arranging study desks, watering plants, and tidying rooms.
2. Care During Illness: When someone falls sick, family members take turns preparing light nutritious meals, giving prescribed medicines on time, and providing comfort.
3. Emotional Bond: Celebrating festivals and overcoming difficulties together strengthens mutual love and emotional security.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Sharing daily chores described 1 M
Care during illness explained 1 M
Emotional bonding and unity 1 M
Q6 What is the key difference between a nuclear family and a joint family? Mention one advantage of each. Diverse Family Structures • Nuclear vs Joint 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Comparison:
• Nuclear Family: Consists only of parents and their children living together. Advantage: Independent decision-making and peaceful privacy.
• Joint Family: Consists of grandparents, parents, uncles, aunts, and cousins living under the same roof. Advantage: Grandparents provide loving guidance, childcare support, and companionship.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear definition of both family structures 1.5 M
Valid advantages stated for both 1.5 M
Q7 How can children show respect and care for elderly grandparents in their home? Respecting Elders • Values 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Caring for Grandparents:
1. Spending quality time listening to their childhood stories and experiences.
2. Helping them find their spectacles, walking sticks, or fetching water and medicines.
3. Accompanying them for morning and evening walks and speaking with polite, patient words.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three practical ways to care for grandparents 3 M
Q8 Why do many families adopt pets (dogs, cats, birds)? What responsibilities come with adopting a pet? Empathy • Pets as Family 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Pet Adoption & Responsibilities:
• Why: Pets provide companionship, love, and loyalty, teaching children empathy and gentle care.
• Responsibilities: Providing clean drinking water, fresh balanced pet food, regular walks, clean living space, and timely veterinary vaccinations.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Emotional importance of pets 1 M
Key pet care responsibilities 1 M
Q9 When siblings or family members disagree on something (like watching TV or playing a game), how should they resolve the conflict peacefully? Conflict Resolution • Harmony 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Peaceful Resolution:
1. Take turns talking calmly without shouting or interrupting.
2. Listen to each other's point of view with patience.
3. Agree on a fair compromise, such as taking turns or choosing an activity both enjoy.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Calm communication emphasized 1 M
Fair compromise and mutual respect 1 M
Q10 What are family traditions, and how do they pass from one generation to the next? Family Traditions • Cultural Heritage 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Family Traditions:
Traditions are special customs, festival recipes, songs, or values practiced regularly by a family. They are passed down as children observe and participate with parents and grandparents during annual celebrations and religious ceremonies.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Definition of family traditions 1 M
Generational transmission explained 1 M
Q11 How should family members support a child or relative who has a visual or hearing impairment? Inclusivity • Special Needs Support 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Supportive Actions:
• Keep pathways clear of clutter and loose wires so they can move safely.
• Learn basic sign language or speak clearly facing the person.
• Encourage them with patience and treat them with equal dignity and love.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Physical safety precautions 1 M
Equal dignity and empathy 1 M
Q12 Why is having a structured daily family routine beneficial for growing children? Daily Routine • Time Management 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Benefits of Routine:
1. Instills discipline for waking up, studying, eating, and sleeping on time.
2. Ensures adequate rest (8-9 hours of sleep) for brain and body growth.
3. Reduces stress and chaos in the morning before school.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Two valid health/discipline benefits 2 M
Q13 What are three eco-friendly habits a family can practice together at home to save electricity and water? Environmental Responsibility • Green Homes 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Eco-Friendly Family Habits:
1. Switch off lights, fans, and appliances when leaving a room.
2. Fix leaking taps immediately and use a bucket for bathing instead of a shower.
3. Segregate dry and wet kitchen waste into separate dustbins.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three practical eco-friendly home habits 3 M
Q14 Write a short thank-you note to one family member expressing appreciation for something special they did for you. Personal Reflection • Expressing Gratitude 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Sample Thank-You Note:
Dear Grandma,
Thank you so much for reading bedtime stories to me and teaching me how to make paper boats during the rainy season. Your warm hugs and delicious carrot halwa always make me feel very happy. I love you!
— Your loving grandchild
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Warm, respectful, and sincere expression of gratitude 2 M
🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Supporting Grandparents with Digital Technology

Real-World Environment Context: Grandfather wants to consult his eye doctor through a telemedicine video call but feels confused by the smartphone screen.

Analytical Task: How can a Class 4 student assist their grandfather respectfully without making him feel helpless?

The student should sit patiently beside grandfather, open the app, adjust the screen brightness and volume, and gently guide grandfather's finger to tap the call button. Explaining each step with kindness builds grandfather's confidence while showing deep filial gratitude.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for patient step-by-step guidance; 1.5 Marks for showing filial respect and dignity.

Unit 1: Our Community • Class 4 EVS (New NEP 2020)

Chapter 2: Exploring Our Neighbourhood

Community Helpers, Public Utilities, Neighborhood Mapping & Civic Cleanliness

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Key public institutions in a neighborhood: Primary health clinic, post office, police station, fire station, bank, and library.
  • Community helpers who maintain civic life: Sanitation workers, electricians, plumbers, farmers, carpenters, and traffic police.
  • Reading simple neighborhood route maps with symbols and landmarks.
  • Civic responsibility: Maintaining clean public parks, segregating wet and dry waste, and preserving public property.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 Name four essential public places in a neighbourhood and explain the primary function of each. Institutional Inquiry • Public Utilities 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Four Essential Public Places:
1. Primary Health Centre / Hospital: Provides first-aid, outpatient medical consultations, life-saving vaccinations, and emergency treatment for sick and injured citizens.
2. Post Office: Delivers letters, parcels, and money orders, and offers secure postal savings schemes and national insurance services.
3. Police Station: Maintains law and order, investigates local crimes, ensures neighborhood security, and assists citizens in distress.
4. Fire Station: Operates specialized fire engines and rescue personnel to extinguish fires, rescue people during building collapses, and manage flood emergencies.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Naming four valid public institutions 2.0 M
Accurate, concise explanation of each institution's function 2.0 M
Q2 What is a 'landmark'? How do cardinal directions (North, South, East, West) and a map key (legend) help us find a place? Mapping & Navigation • Reading Maps 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Landmark:
A landmark is a prominent, well-known, and easily recognizable building or natural feature (like a tall water tank, a large banyan tree, a school, or a temple) that serves as a reference point for finding locations.

2. Cardinal Directions & Map Key:
• Cardinal Directions (N, S, E, W): Give spatial orientation. On standard maps, North is at the top, South at the bottom, East to the right, and West to the left.
• Map Key (Legend): Explains the symbols, colours, and icons used on the map (e.g., a red cross for a hospital, a blue strip for a river, or a tent for a camp).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Definition of landmark with realistic examples 1.5 M
Role of cardinal directions and map legend in spatial navigation 1.5 M
Q3 Why is it important to segregate waste at source into green and blue bins? Give two examples of items that go into each bin. Civic Responsibility • Waste Segregation 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Importance of Segregating at Source:
Segregating waste at home prevents wet biodegradable garbage from mixing with dry recyclable items. Mixed waste rots in open landfills, generating toxic methane gas and groundwater-poisoning leachate. Proper segregation enables composting of wet waste and recycling of dry materials.

2. Bin Classification:
• Green Bin (Wet / Biodegradable Waste): Fruit peels, vegetable scraps, leftover food, tea leaves.
• Blue Bin (Dry / Recyclable Waste): Plastic bottles, cardboard boxes, newspapers, metal cans, glass jars.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Environmental importance of source segregation 1.5 M
Two accurate examples each for green and blue bins 1.5 M
Q4 What do you understand by 'Dignity of Labour'? How should we treat sanitation workers who clean our streets? Social Harmony • Dignity of Labour 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Dignity of Labour:
Dignity of labour means that every honest job and service—whether done by a surgeon, engineer, farmer, or sweeper—deserves equal respect, honour, and fair compensation. No honest work is 'low' or 'dirty'.

2. Treatment of Sanitation Workers:
We must treat sanitation workers with courteous language, greet them respectfully, never litter on streets, hand over properly tied and segregated waste, and support their rights to protective safety gear (gloves, masks, boots).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Concept of dignity of labour explained clearly 1.0 M
Respectful and practical civic conduct toward sanitation workers 1.0 M
Q5 Name three public service institutions located in your neighbourhood and state the main function of each. Public Institutions • Community Helpers 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Neighbourhood Institutions:
1. Primary Health Centre (Hospital): Provides first aid, medical checkups, and vaccinations to sick people.
2. Post Office: Delivers letters, parcels, money orders, and offers small savings bank accounts.
3. Police Station: Maintains law and order, prevents crime, and protects citizens.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three institutions named with accurate civic functions 3 M
Q6 Match the emergency situations with their correct toll-free national emergency helpline numbers in India: Police, Fire Brigade, Ambulance, Childline. Emergency Helplines • Public Safety 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Emergency Numbers:
• Police: 112 / 100
• Fire Brigade: 101
• Ambulance: 102 / 108
• Childline: 1098
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
All emergency numbers correctly identified 2 M
Q7 Why is the work of municipal sanitation workers essential for a healthy neighbourhood? How should we treat them? Sanitation Workers • Dignity of Labour 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Sanitation Workers:
• Importance: They sweep roads, collect domestic garbage, and clear storm drains daily. Without them, rotting waste would spread infectious diseases like cholera and dengue.
• Respect: We must treat them with high dignity and gratitude, hand over segregated waste cleanly, and avoid throwing broken glass or sharp objects loosely.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Role in disease prevention explained 1.5 M
Dignity of labour and safe disposal practices 1.5 M
Q8 State three essential road safety rules that pedestrians must follow while walking in their neighbourhood. Road Safety • Pedestrian Rules 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Pedestrian Safety Rules:
1. Always walk on the footpath; if there is no footpath, walk on the right side facing oncoming traffic.
2. Cross the road only at the Zebra Crossing or pedestrian footbridge after looking right, then left, then right again.
3. Never run across the road or play games near moving traffic.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three distinct road safety guidelines 3 M
Q9 Why are public neighbourhood parks often called 'green lungs' of urban residential areas? Public Parks • Community Wellbeing 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Green Lungs:
Trees and plants in parks absorb carbon dioxide emitted by vehicles and release fresh oxygen. Parks also filter dust, provide open spaces for children to play, and offer elderly citizens a tranquil place for walking and social interaction.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Oxygen release and air purification explained 1 M
Recreational and social benefits 1 M
Q10 What is public property? Give two examples and describe how citizens should protect it. Civic Sense • Public Property 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Public Property:
Facilities created and maintained by the government with public tax funds for everyone's use (e.g., streetlights, park benches, public buses).
Protection: Citizens must never scratch, vandalize, write graffiti, or break these fixtures.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Definition and examples 1 M
Care and anti-vandalism practice 1 M
Q11 If an open manhole or a broken water pipe is spotted on your street, what steps should residents take immediately? Civic Problem Reporting • Grievance Redressal 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Immediate Steps:
1. Place a visible warning sign or branch near the open manhole to alert walkers and drivers.
2. Notify adults and file a prompt complaint with the local Municipal Ward Office or helpline.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Safety warning placement 1 M
Municipal complaint filing 1 M
Q12 How does having neighbours of different cultural, religious, and linguistic backgrounds enrich community life? Neighbourhood Diversity • Social Harmony 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Cultural Enrichment:
Neighbours learn about diverse festival customs, enjoy varied traditional foods, celebrate together, and develop tolerance and unity in diversity.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Mutual cultural learning and unity explained 2 M
Q13 What is a weekly neighbourhood market (haat / bazaar), and how does it support local farmers? Local Markets • Weekly Haat 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Weekly Market (Haat):
A temporary open-air market held on a specific day of the week where local farmers and traders sell fresh seasonal vegetables, fruits, and cookware directly to consumers without middlemen.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Concept of haat explained 1 M
Direct farmer-to-consumer benefit 1 M
Q14 What key symbols and landmarks should you include when drawing a sketch map of the route from your home to school? Mapping • Sketching Neighborhood 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Map Elements:
Include major landmarks (milk booth, temple, crossroad, post office), directional arrows showing turns (left/right), a compass North pointer, and clear symbol legends.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Four essential cartographic elements mentioned 2 M
🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Waste Segregation and Community Composting

Real-World Environment Context: Residents of an apartment society dump mixed garbage in open street corners, attracting stray dogs and foul smell.

Analytical Task: Design an action plan for the resident welfare association to solve this civic problem permanently.

The association should implement a mandatory three-bin system (Green for wet kitchen waste, Blue for dry recyclables, Red for hazardous sanitary/electronic waste). They should set up an on-site aerated composting pit for wet waste to produce rich garden manure, partner with authorized recyclers for dry waste, and install CCTV monitoring to fine repeated open littering.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for source-segregation and composting mechanism; 1.5 Marks for community enforcement and recycling partnership.

Unit 2: Sustenance & Nature • Class 4 EVS (New NEP 2020)

Chapter 3: Nature Trail

Plant Biodiversity, Leaf Variations, Bark Textures, Tree Canopies & Urban Ecology

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Observing plant diversity: Herbs, shrubs, climbers, creepers, and giant perennial trees.
  • Leaf variations: Size, shape (oval, heart-shaped, needle-like), margin (smooth, serrated, lobed), and venation (reticulate vs. parallel).
  • Bark textures and trunk patterns that protect trees from extreme weather, pests, and fire.
  • Ecological benefits of urban trees: Shade, temperature cooling, soil retention, and bird sanctuaries.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is 'leaf venation'? Differentiate between reticulate and parallel venation with two plant examples for each. Botanical Observation • Leaf Venation 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Leaf Venation:
Leaf venation is the design or pattern of veins (tubes carrying water, minerals, and synthesized food) distributed across the lamina (leaf blade).

2. Reticulate vs. Parallel Venation:
• Reticulate Venation: The veins branch out from a prominent central midrib in an irregular web-like or net-like network across the leaf blade. Examples: Peepal, Mango, Neem, Rose, China Rose.
• Parallel Venation: The veins run parallel to one another from the leaf base to the tip without forming a network. Examples: Banana, Grass, Wheat, Maize, Bamboo, Palm.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Definition of venation and function of veins 1.0 M
Precise contrast with 2 correct examples for each venation type 2.0 M
Q2 What is tree bark, and why is it important for the survival of a tree? How does bark vary across different trees? Plant Anatomy • Bark and Trunk 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Function of Tree Bark:
The bark is the outermost protective layer covering the trunk and branches of a woody tree. It acts like a tree's skin, protecting inner living tissues from mechanical injury, extreme heat, severe winter frost, insect attacks, fungal infections, and dehydration.

2. Variations in Bark:
• Rough and Furrowed: Neem, Peepal, and Banyan have thick, deeply cracked, rough bark.
• Smooth and Peeling: Eucalyptus and Silver Birch have smooth bark that sheds in long paper-like strips.
• Spiny Bark: Silk Cotton (Semal) tree trunks bear conical woody prickles for defense.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Protective functions of bark clearly explained 1.5 M
Describing different bark textures with tree examples 1.5 M
Q3 Why are trees called the 'green lungs' of cities? Mention three ways large roadside trees make our cities liveable. Urban Ecology • Benefits of Trees 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why Called Green Lungs:
Trees undergo photosynthesis, absorbing harmful greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and releasing fresh, oxygenated air essential for human and animal respiration. They filter airborne dust and soot particles on their leaf surfaces.

2. Three Ways Trees Make Cities Liveable:
• Temperature Cooling: Transpiration from tree canopies lowers ambient neighborhood temperatures by 2°C to 5°C, reducing the urban heat island effect.
• Noise & Pollution Buffer: Dense roadside foliage absorbs traffic noise and traps vehicle exhaust pollutants.
• Biodiversity Support: Canopies provide nesting grounds and shade for birds, squirrels, butterflies, and pollinators.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of oxygen production and CO2 absorption 1.5 M
Three distinct ecological/urban benefits described 1.5 M
Q4 Describe the step-by-step process of preparing a leaf herbarium sheet for nature study. Practical Activity • Making a Herbarium 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Steps to Prepare a Herbarium Sheet:
1. Collection: Pick fresh, fallen, healthy leaves of different shapes from the ground (avoid tearing living branches).
2. Pressing & Drying: Place the leaves flat between sheets of old newspaper or blotting paper, and place a heavy book on top for 5 to 7 days until all moisture is absorbed.
3. Mounting: Carefully paste the dried, flattened leaves onto a thick chart sheet using small strips of paper tape.
4. Labelling: Write the common name, scientific name, date, location of collection, leaf shape, and venation type beside each specimen.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Four correct sequential steps (collection, pressing, mounting, labelling) 2.0 M
Q5 What are the two main types of venation found in leaves? Give two plant examples of each. Leaf Venation • Scientific Observation 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Types of Venation:
1. Reticulate Venation: Veins form a net-like web pattern throughout the leaf blade. Examples: Peepal, Mango, Hibiscus, Rose.
2. Parallel Venation: Veins run parallel and straight side-by-side from base to tip. Examples: Banana, Grass, Bamboo, Maize.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Reticulate venation defined with examples 1.5 M
Parallel venation defined with examples 1.5 M
Q6 Why do trees have bark, and how can children take a 'bark rubbing' using paper and crayons? Tree Bark • Function & Texture 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Bark & Rubbing Technique:
• Function: Bark is the protective outer 'skin' of a tree trunk that shields it from harsh weather, insects, fungal infections, and fire.
• Bark Rubbing: Hold a plain sheet of paper firmly against the tree trunk. Rub the side of a wax crayon gently over the paper. The unique rough ridge pattern of the bark transfers onto the paper.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Protective function of bark 1.5 M
Bark rubbing method explained 1.5 M
Q7 State one medicinal use for each of the following common plants found in our surroundings: Tulsi, Neem, Mint (Pudina), Aloe Vera. Medicinal Plants • Traditional Knowledge 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Medicinal Uses:
• Tulsi: Leaves boiled in tea relieve cough, cold, and sore throat.
• Neem: Antibacterial leaves heal skin eruptions and repel pests.
• Mint (Pudina): Soothes stomach ache and aids healthy digestion.

Chapter 4: Growing up with Nature

Plant Germination, Animal Life Cycles, Pet Care & Behavioral Adaptations

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Conditions for seed germination: Water, oxygen/air, suitable temperature, and viable cotyledons.
  • The developmental stages of a plant: Seed coat rupture, radicle (root) emergence, plumule (shoot) growth, and true leaves.
  • Life cycles in animals: Complete metamorphosis in butterflies (egg, larva, pupa, adult) vs. direct development in mammals.
  • Compassionate pet care, responsible feeding, hygienic housing, and recognizing distress signals in animals.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 What conditions are necessary for a bean seed to germinate? Explain the role of the radicle and plumule. Scientific Inquiry • Seed Germination 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Necessary Conditions for Germination:
• Water (Moisture): Softens the tough seed coat and activates dormant growth enzymes.
• Air (Oxygen): Needed for cellular respiration to generate energy for cell division.
• Warmth (Suitable Temperature): Optimum warmth allows biochemical reactions to proceed smoothly. (Light is generally not required until leaves appear).

2. Role of Radicle and Plumule:
• Radicle: The embryonic root that grows downward into the soil (positive geotropism) to anchor the seedling and absorb water and dissolved minerals.
• Plumule: The embryonic shoot that grows upward toward sunlight (positive phototropism) to develop stems, leaves, and flowers.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three vital environmental factors for germination 1.5 M
Correct biological functions of radicle and plumule 1.5 M
Q2 Describe the four stages in the life cycle of a butterfly. Why does the caterpillar eat voraciously? Life Cycles • Metamorphosis 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Four Stages of Butterfly Life Cycle (Metamorphosis):
1. Egg: Laid by the adult female butterfly on the underside of a host plant's leaf.
2. Larva (Caterpillar): Hatches from the egg; worm-like, with chewing mouthparts.
3. Pupa (Chrysalis): The caterpillar spins a protective cocoon or shell around itself; inside, dramatic organ reorganization takes place.
4. Adult Butterfly: Emerges with wings and siphoning mouthparts to feed on flower nectar and reproduce.

2. Why Caterpillars Eat Voraciously:
The caterpillar needs to store immense energy and nutrients because during the pupa stage, it cannot eat at all. All the energy required to grow wings, legs, and antennae comes from the food consumed during the larval stage.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate description of all four stages 2.5 M
Biological reasoning for the caterpillar's intense feeding 1.5 M
Q3 What responsibilities must a family take when adopting a domestic pet (like a dog or cat)? Animal Welfare • Responsible Pet Care 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Responsibilities of Pet Ownership:
1. Nutritious Food & Clean Water: Providing species-appropriate, balanced meals at fixed intervals and 24/7 access to fresh drinking water.
2. Veterinary Health: Timely vaccinations (especially anti-rabies), regular deworming, and prompt medical check-ups when sick.
3. Hygienic Living Space: A clean, dry, well-ventilated shelter with protection from extreme cold or summer heat.
4. Exercise & Affection: Daily walking, playtime, and gentle, loving interaction without teasing or physical cruelty.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Four comprehensive dimensions of pet care (food, health, shelter, affection) 3.0 M
Q4 How does the growth of a mango tree differ from the growth of a puppy? State two key differences. Comparative Biology • Plant vs. Animal Growth 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Differences in Growth:
1. Locational vs. Proportionate Growth: A plant grows only at specific growing tips (meristems at root tips and stem tips), whereas a puppy grows uniformly across all body parts simultaneously.
2. Duration of Growth: A tree can continue to grow new branches, leaves, and rings of wood throughout its life (indeterminate growth), while a puppy stops growing in height and length once it reaches adult maturity (determinate growth).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Two accurate, scientifically valid differences in growth patterns 2.0 M
Q5 Describe the four distinct stages in the life cycle of a butterfly. What is metamorphosis? Life Cycle • Butterfly Metamorphosis 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Stages of Butterfly Life Cycle:
1. Egg: Laid on the underside of green leaves.
2. Larva (Caterpillar): Hatches and eats leaves hungrily, growing rapidly.
3. Pupa (Chrysalis): Caterpillar spins a protective cocoon around itself and rests while undergoing internal transformation.
4. Adult Butterfly: Emerges with colourful wings.
• Metamorphosis: The dramatic transformation of an immature form into an adult in distinct stages.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

Tadpole vs Adult Frog:
• Tadpole: Lives entirely in water, has a swimming tail, no legs, and breathes dissolved oxygen through gills.
• Adult Frog: Has strong jumping legs, no tail, and breathes through lungs on land and moist skin underwater.

Chapter 5: Food for Health

Nutrition, Digestion, Cooking Methods, Traditional Preservation & Safe Water

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The major nutrient groups: Carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, dietary fibre (roughage), and water.
  • The journey of food: Ploughing, sowing, irrigating, harvesting, storage in mandis, distribution, and cooking.
  • Cooking techniques and nutrient preservation: Boiling, steaming, roasting, shallow frying, and fermentation.
  • Food preservation principles: Sun-drying, salting, sugaring, pickling, and refrigeration to prevent microbial spoilage.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is a 'balanced diet'? Name the three major functional groups of food and provide two food sources for each. Nutritional Science • Balanced Diet 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Balanced Diet:
A balanced diet is a meal plan that contains all essential nutrients (carbohydrates, proteins, fats, vitamins, minerals, roughage, and water) in the right quantities required for growth, tissue repair, disease defense, and daily physical activity.

2. Three Functional Food Groups:
• Energy-Giving Foods (Carbohydrates & Fats): Supply instant and stored energy. Sources: Rice, wheat, potatoes, bananas, butter, ghee, nuts.
• Body-Building Foods (Proteins): Build muscles, repair worn-out cells, and promote height growth. Sources: Pulses, milk, paneer, eggs, fish, soybean.
• Protective Foods (Vitamins & Minerals): Boost immunity, protect against infections, and keep eyes, skin, and bones healthy. Sources: Green leafy vegetables (spinach), citrus fruits, carrots, papaya.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific definition of a balanced diet 1.0 M
Clear categorization of 3 groups with 2 correct sources each 3.0 M
Q2 Why do we cook food before eating? Why is steaming considered healthier than deep frying? Culinary Science • Cooking Methods 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Reasons for Cooking Food:
• Kills harmful disease-causing bacteria and parasites present in raw ingredients.
• Breaks down complex starches and tough plant fibers, making food soft, palatable, and easily digestible.
• Enhances taste, aroma, texture, and visual appeal.

2. Steaming vs. Deep Frying:
• Steaming cooks food gently using water vapour without submerging it in oil. It retains delicate water-soluble vitamins (like Vitamin C and B-complex) and natural flavours without adding unhealthy cholesterol.
• Deep frying exposes food to extreme heat, destroying vitamins and loading the food with excess trans-fats and calories that cause obesity and digestive sluggishness.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three solid reasons why food is cooked 1.5 M
Nutritional contrast between steaming and deep frying 1.5 M
Q3 Explain three traditional methods of preserving food at home. How do they prevent food spoilage? Food Preservation • Methods & Principles 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Three Traditional Preservation Methods:
1. Sun-Drying (Dehydration): Removing all moisture content from foods by spreading them in strong sunlight. Without moisture, bacteria and fungi cannot grow. Examples: Raw mango slices (amchur), red chillies, papads.
2. Pickling in Salt & Mustard Oil: High salt draws out water from microbial cells (osmosis), and an oil layer on top blocks contact with airborne oxygen, preventing bacterial multiplication. Examples: Mango, lemon, and amla pickles.
3. Sugar Syrupping: Storing boiled fruits in thick, concentrated sugar syrup where microbes cannot survive due to high osmotic pressure. Examples: Murabba, fruit jams.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Naming three distinct traditional preservation methods 1.5 M
Scientific principle of microbial inhibition explained for each 1.5 M
Q4 What precautions should be taken to ensure that drinking water is completely safe from contamination? Food Hygiene • Safe Handling 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Precautions for Safe Drinking Water:
1. Boiling: Boiling water vigorously for at least 10–15 minutes kills all bacteria, viruses, and amoebic cysts.
2. Covered Storage: Always store drinking water in clean, covered vessels or earthen pots fitted with a tap.
3. No Hand Dipping: Never dip unwashed fingers or glasses directly into storage pots; always use a clean, long-handled ladle or tap.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Mentioning boiling and two hygienic handling/storage rules 2.0 M

Chapter 6: Happy and Healthy Living

Personal Hygiene, Handwashing Drills, Dental Care, Sleep Rhythms & Mental Well-Being

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Microbiology of everyday germs: How bacteria and viruses spread through unwashed hands and infected surfaces.
  • The WHO 6-step handwashing technique using soap and running water for at least 20 seconds.
  • Dental anatomy and oral health: Enamel, plaque prevention, correct brushing techniques, and cavity avoidance.
  • Restorative sleep rhythms, outdoor physical play, managing stress through yoga and mindfulness, and screen-time balance.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why is washing hands with soap and water more effective than using water alone? When should you mandatorily wash your hands? Preventive Hygiene • Handwashing Drill 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why Soap is Essential:
Water alone cannot dissolve grease, oils, and dirt where germs cling. Soap molecules have two ends: a water-loving head and an oil-loving tail. The oil-loving tails trap the grease and rip open the protective fatty membranes of viruses and bacteria, washing them away down the drain under running water.

2. Mandatory Handwashing Occasions:
• Before preparing, serving, or eating meals.
• Immediately after using the toilet.
• After blowing your nose, coughing, or sneezing into your hands.
• After playing outdoors, touching pets, or handling trash.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific explanation of soap action on germs 1.5 M
Four critical daily handwashing moments 1.5 M
Q2 How do dental cavities form? List three golden rules to keep teeth and gums healthy. Oral Anatomy • Dental Care 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. How Cavities Form:
When sweet, sticky food particles remain lodged between teeth, bacteria living in the mouth feed on these sugars and produce corrosive acids. These acids gradually dissolve tooth enamel (the hard outer protective layer), creating hollow holes called cavities or tooth decay.

2. Three Golden Rules for Dental Health:
• Brush Twice Daily: Brush teeth thoroughly in gentle circular motions for two minutes every morning and before bed.
• Clean Tongue & Rinse: Use a tongue cleaner to remove bacterial film and rinse mouth vigorously with water after every meal.
• Limit Sugary Snacks: Avoid excessive chocolates, sticky candies, and sugary soft drinks; eat crunchy foods like apples and carrots that clean teeth naturally.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific process of plaque and acid cavity formation 1.5 M
Three practical rules for long-term dental hygiene 1.5 M
Q3 Why do growing children need 8 to 9 hours of uninterrupted sleep every night? What happens if you have poor posture? Physiology & Rest • Sleep & Posture 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Importance of Sound Sleep:
During deep sleep, the brain releases growth hormones, repairs body tissues, organizes daytime memories, and strengthens immune defenses. Inadequate sleep leads to morning fatigue, poor concentration in school, irritability, and weakened immunity.

2. Consequences of Poor Posture:
Slouching, bending over desks, or looking down at screens for long periods strains spinal muscles, causes neck and back pain, compresses the chest (reducing lung capacity), and can lead to permanent spinal curvature.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Physiological benefits of deep sleep in children 1.5 M
Physical hazards of slouching and bad sitting posture 1.5 M
Q4 What is 'screen fatigue'? Suggest two healthy outdoor alternatives to spending hours on mobile phones. Mental Health • Screen Time Balance 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Screen Fatigue:
Screen fatigue refers to the eye strain, headaches, dry eyes, neck stiffness, and mental exhaustion caused by continuously staring at digital screens (smartphones, tablets, TVs) for hours without blinking adequately.

2. Healthy Outdoor Alternatives:
• Playing team sports like football, badminton, or kho-kho with neighbourhood friends to build physical stamina.
• Cycling in community parks or engaging in gardening and observing nature trails.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear explanation of screen fatigue symptoms 1.0 M

Q5 Describe the proper 6-step handwashing technique recommended by doctors. When should we always wash hands? Personal Hygiene • WHO Handwashing Method 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
6-Step Handwashing Method:
1. Wet hands and apply soap.
2. Rub palms together.
3. Rub back of each hand with interlaced fingers.
4. Clean between fingers and thumbs.
5. Clean back of fingers and fingertips under palms.
6. Clean wrists, rinse thoroughly under running water, and dry with a clean towel.
• When to wash: Before eating, after using the toilet, and after touching pets.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

Chapter 7: How Things Work

Simple Machines: Levers, Pulleys, Wheels & Axles, Inclined Planes & Mechanics

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The six classical simple machines: Lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, wedge, and screw.
  • The mechanical advantage of levers: Understanding the interplay between Fulcrum, Load, and Effort (e.g., scissors, see-saw, bottle opener).
  • Pulleys in daily life: Fixed pulleys for drawing water from wells and hoisting national flags.
  • Friction as a necessary force: Why vehicles need friction to brake, why soles have grooves, and how lubrication reduces wear and tear.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is a 'simple machine'? Name any four simple machines and give one everyday tool based on each. Physics Principles • Simple Machines 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Simple Machine:
A simple machine is a mechanical device with few or no moving parts that makes work easier, faster, or safer by multiplying applied force, increasing speed, or changing the direction of force.

2. Four Simple Machines and Examples:
• Lever: A rigid bar rotating around a pivot (fulcrum). Example: Scissors, see-saw, crowbar, bottle opener.
• Pulley: A grooved wheel with a rope running around it to lift loads. Example: Flagpole hoisting rig, well-water pulley, crane hook.
• Inclined Plane: A sloping surface that connects a lower level to a higher level. Example: Hospital wheelchair ramp, truck loading plank, slide.
• Wheel and Axle: A large wheel rigidly attached to a central smaller rod. Example: Doorknob, steering wheel, bicycle pedal.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific definition of a simple machine 1.0 M
Four distinct simple machines with correct everyday examples 3.0 M
Q2 How does a fixed pulley help in drawing water from a deep village well? Why is pulling downwards easier than lifting straight up? Mechanical Systems • The Pulley 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. How a Fixed Pulley Works:
A fixed pulley consists of a grooved wheel hung securely from a wooden beam directly over the well mouth. A long, strong rope is threaded through the groove; one end is tied to the water bucket and the other end is held by the person.

2. Why Pulling Downward is Easier:
When lifting a bucket straight up without a pulley, a person must fight gravity directly with only arm muscles. With a fixed pulley, the direction of force is reversed to pulling downwards. This allows the person to use their own body weight to help pull the rope down, making the work feel substantially easier and safer.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Mechanics of the well pulley described clearly 1.5 M
Explanation of force redirection and using body weight against gravity 1.5 M
Q3 Why is friction called a 'necessary evil'? Give one example where friction is helpful and one where it causes a problem. Forces in Action • Friction 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why Called a Necessary Evil:
Friction is called a necessary evil because life would be impossible without it (we could not walk, write, or stop cars), yet it constantly wastes valuable energy by producing unwanted heat, noise, and mechanical wear and tear.

2. Examples:
• Helpful Friction: The deep treads on bicycle and car tyres provide grip on wet roads, preventing dangerous skidding and allowing brakes to stop the vehicle.
• Harmful Friction: Friction between the moving metal parts of a sewing machine or bicycle chain grinds down the metal and causes squeaking; requiring periodic oiling or grease lubrication.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Explanation of dual nature (useful vs. wasteful) 1.5 M
One valid example each for helpful and harmful friction 1.5 M
Q4 How can you construct a simple working beam balance using a plastic ruler, thread, and paper cups? Hands-on Science • Making a Balance 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Construction of a Simple Beam Balance:
1. Pivot (Fulcrum): Punch a tiny hole at the exact centre (15 cm mark) of a 30 cm plastic ruler and suspend it with a looped piece of thread from a stationary hook so it hangs horizontally balanced.
2. Pans: Punch three equidistant holes near the rims of two identical paper cups. Tie three equal-length threads to each cup and hang one cup at the 2 cm mark and the other at the 28 cm mark.
3. Operation: When both pans are empty, the ruler stays level. Place an unknown object (like an eraser) in one pan and known standard units (like metal paper clips or identical coins) in the other pan until the ruler balances horizontally.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear three-step construction of pivot, pans, and balancing measurement 2.0 M

Q7 Why does a small iron nail sink in water, while a huge iron ship floats safely on the ocean? Buoyancy • Floating and Sinking 3 Marks

Buoyancy Principle:
An iron nail is solid and dense; it displaces very little water, so the upward buoyant water force is less than its weight, causing it to sink. A ship is hollowed out inside with vast air pockets; its large volume displaces a huge weight of water, creating an upward buoyant force equal to the ship's total weight.

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Designing Accessible Wheelchair Ramps for Public Buildings

Real-World Environment Context: A village community centre has a 4-step staircase (height 60 cm). An elderly resident in a wheelchair cannot enter.

Analytical Task: Apply the principle of an inclined plane to calculate the recommended length of an accessible ramp.

According to universal accessible design standards, the slope of a wheelchair ramp should be gentle, ideally a 1:12 ratio (for every 1 unit of rise, 12 units of horizontal run are required). For a vertical height of 60 cm (0.6 m), the ramp length should be at least 0.6 m × 12 = 7.2 metres, equipped with sturdy handrails and non-slip surface ridges to allow effortless manual wheelchair ascent.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for 1:12 slope ratio calculation (7.2 m); 1.5 Marks for safety handrails and non-skid surface features.

Chapter 8: How Things are Made

Artisanal Crafts: Pottery, Handloom Weaving, Carpentry, Metal Casting & Indian Guilds

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Traditional Indian craft traditions: Terracotta pottery, handloom textiles, wood carving, and metal casting.
  • The stages of pottery: Digging clay, kneading to remove air bubbles, shaping on the potter's wheel, sun-drying, firing in a kiln (bhatti), and painting.
  • Handloom weaving: The interlacing of lengthwise threads (warp) and crosswise threads (weft) on a wooden loom.
  • Carpentry tools and techniques: Sawing, chiselling, planing, joinery, and sandpaper finishing.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 Describe the step-by-step process of making an earthen pitcher (matka) on a potter's wheel. Why must the pot be baked in a kiln? Traditional Crafts • Pottery Process 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Steps in Making a Matka:
1. Clay Preparation: Fine, sticky riverbed clay is dug up, stones and grit are sifted out, and water is mixed in.
2. Kneading: The wet clay is kneaded vigorously with hands and feet to remove air bubbles and create uniform plasticity.
3. Shaping on Wheel: A lump of clay is centered on the spinning potter's wheel. The potter uses skilled fingers and water to hollow and pull up the walls into a round pot shape.
4. Beating & Sun-Drying: The bottom is beaten with a wooden mallet (thapa) and stone anvil (pindi) to make the base round and strong, then dried in the shade and sun.

2. Why Kiln Baking is Essential:
Unbaked sun-dried clay pots dissolve back into mud as soon as water is poured into them. Baking pots inside a high-temperature brick kiln (bhatti) causes irreversible chemical fusion of silica particles, turning the clay into hard, permanent, porous, and waterproof terracotta.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Sequential four-step pottery making process 2.5 M
Scientific reason for kiln baking and terracotta transformation 1.5 M
Q2 What is the difference between 'warp' and 'weft' in weaving cloth on a loom? Textile Crafts • Handloom Weaving 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Warp vs. Weft:
• Warp (तानी): The set of long, parallel threads stretched lengthwise tightly on the wooden loom frame from front to back.
• Weft (भरनी): The crosswise thread wound on a bobbin inside a flying shuttle that is passed back and forth horizontally through the separated warp threads.
The tight interlocking of warp and weft threads produces the continuous fabric of a saree, shawl, or cloth sheet.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear, correct definition of lengthwise warp threads 1.5 M
Clear, correct definition of crosswise weft threads and shuttle 1.5 M

2. Chisel (Rookhani / Chheeni): A beveled steel blade used with a wooden mallet to carve mortises, grooves, and artistic designs into wood.
3. Hand Plane (Randa): A wooden or metal tool with an adjustable blade used to shave off rough bumps and make wooden planks completely flat and smooth.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

Chapter 9: Different Lands, Different Lives

Geographical Diversity of India: Mountains, Deserts, Coastal Plains & River Valleys

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The major physical divisions of India: Northern Mountains (Himalayas), Great Indian Desert (Thar), Coastal Plains, and Deccan Plateau.
  • Climate adaptations in shelter: Sloping roofs in snow and rain zones; thick mud walls and flat roofs in arid deserts; stilt houses in flood-prone river plains.
  • Traditional livelihoods shaped by local topography: Terrace farming, sheep rearing, coastal fishing, date-palm cultivation, and river transport.
  • Rich cultural unity amidst vast linguistic, dietary, and architectural diversity across India.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why do houses in the hilly regions of Himachal Pradesh and Kashmir have steeply sloping roofs, while houses in the Thar Desert of Rajasthan have thick mud walls and flat roofs? Geographical Adaptation • Architecture 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Houses in Hilly Regions (Himachal Pradesh & Kashmir):
These areas experience heavy monsoon rains and freezing winter snowfall. Sloping roofs made of corrugated iron sheets or slate tiles allow rainwater and heavy snow to slide off immediately without accumulating on the roof. This prevents roof collapse, water leakage, and dampness.

2. Houses in the Thar Desert (Rajasthan):
The desert climate experiences scorching daytime temperatures exceeding 45°C. Thick mud walls act as excellent natural insulators, preventing outside heat from penetrating into living rooms during the day. Flat roofs are used to sleep under open starlit skies at night when desert sands cool down, and for drying grains and chillies.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Detailed reasoning for sloping roofs in snow/rain hill zones 2.0 M
Detailed reasoning for thick mud insulation and flat roofs in deserts 2.0 M
Q2 What is 'terrace farming' (step farming)? Why is it practiced predominantly in mountainous regions? Regional Livelihoods • Terrace Farming 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Terrace Farming:
Terrace farming is an agricultural method where steep mountain slopes are cut into a series of broad, flat horizontal step-like terraces supported by stone retaining walls.

2. Why Practiced in Mountains:
• On steep mountain slopes, heavy rainfall rushes down rapidly, washing away the fertile topsoil (soil erosion).
• By creating flat step terraces, the velocity of runoff water is slowed down, allowing water to soak in and retain fertile soil so crops like tea, rice, and maize can grow successfully.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate physical definition of step terraces 1.5 M
Prevention of soil erosion and water retention explained 1.5 M
Q3 Why are houses in rural Assam built on tall bamboo stilts 10 to 12 feet above the ground? Flood Adaptation • Stilt Houses 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Reasons for Stilt Houses in Assam:
1. Severe Monsoon Floods: Assam receives torrential monsoon rainfall causing the mighty Brahmaputra river and its tributaries to flood vast plains every year. Raising houses 10–12 feet on strong bamboo or timber stilts keeps floodwaters from entering living rooms.
2. Protection from Dangerous Animals: Stilts prevent venomous snakes, leeches, scorpions, and wild animals displaced by floodwaters from entering the home.
3. Abundant Bamboo: Bamboo grows abundantly in northeastern forests and is durable, lightweight, resilient, and water-resistant.

Q4 What does 'Unity in Diversity' mean in the context of India? Give two examples of how diverse cultures celebrate together. Cultural Geography • Unity in Diversity 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Meaning of Unity in Diversity:
It means that despite having thousands of languages, diverse cuisines, distinct traditional dresses, and varied geographical landscapes, all Indians share a deep common bond of national identity, mutual respect, and shared constitutional brotherhood.

2. Examples of Shared Celebrations:
• Harvest festivals celebrated nationwide under different regional names during the same week of January: Makar Sankranti (North & West), Pongal (Tamil Nadu), Bihu (Assam), and Lohri (Punjab).

Accurate definition of Unity in Diversity 1.0 M

Q5 Why do houses in hilly areas like Himachal Pradesh and Kashmir have steeply sloping roofs, while houses in Rajasthan have flat roofs? Climate Architecture • Sloping vs Flat Roofs 3 Marks

Roof Design Adaptations:

• Hot Deserts (Rajasthan): Flat roofs are used to sleep under open night skies, dry food grains, and collect scarce rainwater.

Assam experiences torrential monsoon rainfall and seasonal flooding from the Brahmaputra River. Raising houses on strong bamboo or wooden stilts prevents floodwaters from entering living rooms and keeps wild animals and snakes away.

Q7 How do thick mud walls and thatched roofs keep houses in rural Rajasthan naturally cool during extreme summer heat? Desert Living • Mud Insulation 3 Marks

Thermal Insulation of Mud:

Water Habitats of Kashmir:

Attire Adaptations:

• Kerala: People wear light, breathable white cotton Mundu and sarees to stay comfortable in humid, tropical coastal weather.

Igloos:
An igloo is a dome-shaped winter shelter constructed from compressed blocks of packed snow. Packed snow contains trapped air pockets, which act as an excellent thermal insulator, trapping body heat inside.

Description of igloo 1 M

Nomadic Tents:
Nomads are people who do not stay permanently in one place, moving seasonally with their animal herds to find fresh grazing pastures. They live in strong, portable yak-hair tents (Rebo) that can be packed and pitched easily.

Definition of nomads 1 M
Portability and yak-hair protection explained 1 M
Q12 How does life for children living in coastal fishing villages (like Andaman and Nicobar Islands) revolve around the sea? Island Communities • Coastal Life 2 Marks

Children learn swimming, canoeing, and predicting sea weather from an early age. Fish and coconuts form the staple diet, and families build stilt homes with woven palm thatch.

Q13 Why do farmers in hilly mountain slopes build stepped terrace farms? Mountain Farming • Step Terraces 2 Marks

Terrace Farming:
Steep slopes cause rainwater to wash away fertile topsoil rapidly. Carving flat horizontal steps (terraces) along hills slows water runoff and retains water and soil for rice cultivation.

Soil erosion prevention and water retention 2 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Preserving the Living Root Bridges of Meghalaya

Real-World Environment Context: The Khasi and Jaintia tribes of Meghalaya grow pedestrian bridges across fast mountain torrents using living rubber tree roots.

Analytical Task: Analyze why living root bridges are far superior to modern concrete or steel bridges in torrential rainforest valleys.

Unlike concrete or iron bridges that rust, rot, and get washed away by torrential monsoon floods, living root bridges made from Ficus elastica roots grow stronger and thicker over decades as the living tree continues to anchor deeper into riverbanks. They require no cement, cost zero money, cause no carbon emissions, and can endure for over 500 years in humid rainforest ecosystems.

Chapter 10: Our Sky

The Solar System, Earth's Rotation & Revolution, Moon Phases & Constellations

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The celestial sphere: Sun, Moon, stars, constellations, and artificial observation satellites.
  • Day and Night mechanics: Earth's 24-hour rotation from West to East around its tilted axis.
  • The changing phases of the Moon: 29.5-day synodic cycle from New Moon (Amavasya) to Full Moon (Purnima).
  • Finding directions using the night sky: Saptarshi (Big Dipper) and Dhruva Tara (Pole Star).
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (14 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why do day and night occur on Earth? Why does the Moon appear to change its shape every night throughout the month? Astronomy & Planetary Science 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why Day and Night occur:
The Earth is a spherical planet that rotates on its tilted axis from West to East once every 24 hours. As it rotates, only one half of the Earth faces the Sun at any given time, experiencing Day. The opposite half faces away into shadow, experiencing Night. As the Earth keeps spinning continuously, day and night follow each other smoothly.

2. Why the Moon's shape appears to change (Phases of the Moon):
The Moon does not produce any light of its own; it reflects sunlight like a mirror. As the Moon orbits around the Earth once every 29.5 days, the angle between the Sun, Earth, and Moon changes constantly. From Earth, we can only see that portion of the sunlit half of the Moon that faces us. When none of the sunlit side faces Earth, it is a New Moon (Amavasya); when the entire illuminated side faces us, it is a Full Moon (Purnima).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific explanation of Earth's 24-hour rotation causing day/night 2.0 M
Explanation of Moon reflecting sunlight and orbital angle phases 2.0 M
Q2 What is a 'constellation'? Describe the Saptarshi (Ursa Major) constellation and explain how it helps locate the Pole Star. Sky Observation • Constellations 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Constellation:
A constellation is a recognizable pattern or group of bright stars in the night sky that people historically associated with mythological figures, animals, or objects.

2. Saptarshi & Locating the Pole Star:
• Saptarshi (Big Dipper / Ursa Major): Consists of seven prominent bright stars arranged in the shape of a large ladle or dipper (four stars forming the cup and three stars forming the curved handle).
• Locating Dhruva Tara (Pole Star): The two front stars of the cup are called Pointer Stars. If an imaginary straight line is extended upward through these two pointer stars by about five times the distance between them, it points directly to the Pole Star (North Star), which always marks true geographic North.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Definition of constellation 1.0 M
Description of Saptarshi's seven stars and pointer line to Pole Star 2.0 M
Q3 How does the length and direction of a tree's shadow change from morning to evening? How did people use sundials in ancient times? Solar Motion • Shadows & Time 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Daily Shadow Patterns:
• Early Morning: The Sun is low in the eastern sky, creating very long shadows pointing West.
• Noon (Midday): The Sun reaches its highest point directly overhead, casting the shortest shadow of the day.
• Late Evening: The Sun sinks low in the western sky, casting long shadows pointing East.

2. Ancient Sundials:
Ancient astronomers (like Maharaja Jai Singh at Jantar Mantar) built large triangular ramps called gnomons that cast shadows on calibrated curved marble scales. As the Sun traversed the sky, the moving shadow position accurately indicated the exact hour and minute of the day.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear daily progression of shadow length and direction 1.5 M
Principle of sundial timekeeping explained 1.5 M
Q4 Why must you NEVER look directly at the Sun with naked eyes or through ordinary binoculars, even during a solar eclipse? Safety in Astronomy • Solar Observation 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Danger of Direct Solar Viewing:
The Sun emits intense, focused ultraviolet (UV) and infrared rays. Staring directly at the Sun—or focusing its light through magnifying binoculars or telescopes—burns the light-sensitive retinal cells at the back of the eye (solar retinopathy) in a matter of seconds without causing pain. This can lead to permanent blind spots or complete, incurable blindness. One must only use certified ISO 12312-2 solar filter glasses or pinhole projection methods.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific explanation of retinal burn / UV damage and safe viewing methods 2.0 M
Q5 How are day and night formed on Earth? Explain with a simple globe and torch experiment. Celestial Mechanics • Day and Night 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Day and Night Formation:
Earth is a sphere that rotates continuously on its tilted axis from West to East once every 24 hours.
• Experiment: Shine a torch (representing the Sun) on a globe (representing Earth) in a dark room. The half facing the torch receives light and experiences Day. The opposite half in shadow experiences Night. As the globe turns, day and night alternate.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Rotation of Earth every 24 hours cited 1.5 M
Globe and torch experiment described 1.5 M
Q6 Why does the shape of the Moon appear to change every night? Name four distinct phases of the Moon. Lunar Phases • Moon Cycle 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Phases of the Moon:
The Moon does not produce its own light; it reflects sunlight. As the Moon orbits around Earth, we see differing amounts of its sunlit half from Earth.
Four Phases:
1. New Moon (Amavasya): Moon is between Earth and Sun; dark side faces Earth.
2. Crescent Moon: A tiny curved sliver of light.
3. Half Moon (First/Last Quarter): Half the lit face is visible.
4. Full Moon (Purnima): Entire round sunlit face shines brightly.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Reflected sunlight and orbit explained 2 M
Four lunar phases correctly named 2 M
Q7 Why is the Sun called the ultimate source of light and energy for all life on planet Earth? Solar Energy • The Sun 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
The Sun as Ultimate Source:
1. Photosynthesis: Green plants use sunlight to produce food and oxygen, supporting all herbivores and carnivores.
2. Weather & Water Cycle: Solar heat evaporates water to form rain clouds and drives wind currents.
3. Warmth: Without solar heat, Earth would freeze into an uninhabitable ice planet.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Photosynthesis role explained 1 M
Water cycle / weather driver 1 M
Thermal life support 1 M
Q8 What is a constellation? Describe the Saptarshi (Ursa Major / Great Bear) constellation. Constellations • Saptarshi (Big Dipper) 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Constellations:
• Constellation: A recognizable pattern or group of bright stars in the night sky forming imaginary shapes of animals, mythological heroes, or objects.
• Saptarshi: A group of seven prominent stars resembling a giant saucepan or dipper (four stars form the bowl and three form the curved handle).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific definition of constellation 1.5 M
Saptarshi seven stars and saucepan shape 1.5 M
Q9 How can you find the North direction on a clear night using the pointer stars of Saptarshi? Direction Finding • Pole Star (Dhruva Tara) 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Locating the Pole Star:
Look at the two stars forming the outer front wall of the Saptarshi's bowl (Pointer Stars). Imagine a straight line drawn through them and extended five times their distance upwards. This imaginary line leads directly to the Pole Star (Dhruva Tara), which always indicates true North.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Pointer stars identified 1.5 M
Line projection to Pole Star (North) 1.5 M
Q10 Why should we never look directly at the Sun or during a solar eclipse with naked eyes? Solar Safety • Viewing Eclipses 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Solar Eye Safety:
Intense solar ultraviolet (UV) and infrared radiation can permanently burn the sensitive retinal cells of our eyes, causing irreversible blindness. We must only use certified solar eclipse safety glasses or pinhole projection.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Retinal burn / UV damage explained 1 M
Certified solar filters stated 1 M
Q11 State two differences between a star and a planet that can be observed in the night sky. Astronomy • Planets vs Stars 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Stars vs Planets:
• Stars: Massive balls of burning gas that emit their own light; they appear to twinkle due to atmospheric refraction.
• Planets: Solid or gaseous bodies that reflect sunlight; they shine with steady, non-twinkling light.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Own light vs reflected light 1 M
Twinkling vs steady light 1 M
Q12 Why does the daytime sky appear blue to our eyes on a clear sunny day? Atmosphere • Blue Sky 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Why Sky is Blue:
White sunlight contains all rainbow colors. As light passes through Earth's atmosphere, tiny gas molecules scatter the shorter, blue light waves much more strongly in all directions than other colors.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Atmospheric scattering of short blue wavelengths 2 M
Q13 When and where does a rainbow appear in the sky? What causes its seven colors? Atmospheric Phenomenon • Rainbow 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Rainbow Formation:
A rainbow appears when sunlight shines while rain is falling, always in the sky opposite to the Sun. Tiny suspended raindrops act like microscopic glass prisms that refract, reflect, and disperse white sunlight into its seven constituent colors (VIBGYOR).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Opposite to Sun condition 1 M
Raindrop dispersion of light into VIBGYOR 1 M
Q14 What is an artificial satellite? Mention two ways satellites help people in their everyday lives. Space Exploration • Satellites 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Artificial Satellites:
Human-made spacecraft launched by rockets that orbit Earth.
Everyday Uses:
1. Weather Forecasting: Tracking cyclones and storms to issue early disaster warnings.
2. Communication & GPS: Enabling television broadcasts, mobile phone networks, and vehicle navigation maps.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Definition of artificial satellite 1 M
Weather warnings and GPS navigation uses 2 M

Night Sky Navigation Using the Pole Star

Real-World Environment Context: Ancient sailors and desert travelers had no compass or GPS. On dark clear nights, they never got lost.

Analytical Task: How did travelers locate true North in the night sky using the Saptarshi (Big Dipper) constellation?

Travelers located the seven bright stars of Saptarshi (Ursa Major). The two stars forming the outer front wall of the 'dipper cup' are called the Pointer Stars. Drawing an imaginary straight line through these two pointer stars and extending it five times upward leads directly to a bright, steady star called the Pole Star (Dhruva Tara), which always points to true geographic North.

Chapter 1: Going to School

Transport Modes Across India: Bamboo Bridges, Trolleys, Vallam, Camel Carts & Jugaad

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Different ways children travel to school across geographical terrains in India.
  • Assam: Walking on elevated bamboo and rope bridges across flooded streams.
  • Ladakh: Crossing deep canyons using a wooden trolley pulling along a fixed iron rope with pulleys.
  • Kerala: Traveling in small wooden boats called 'Vallam' to cross backwater canals.
  • Rajasthan (Camel carts), Gujarat (Jugaad vehicle powered by motorcycle engine), and Uttarakhand (rocky mountain paths).
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 How do children in Ladakh reach their school across wide and deep rivers? What is a 'Vallam', and in which state of India is it used? Geographical Adaptation • Transport 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. School Travel in Ladakh:
In Ladakh, rivers are very wide and deep. Children cross them using a strong wooden trolley (an open box with seats). A thick, strong iron rope is tied securely to giant rocks or sturdy trees on both river banks. A pulley rolls over the iron rope, pulling the trolley carrying four to five children smoothly across the canyon.

2. Vallam:
A 'Vallam' is a small traditional wooden boat used in parts of Kerala to help children cross backwater lagoons, rivers, and canals to reach school.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Detailed explanation of Ladakh trolley and pulley system 1.5 M
Definition of Vallam and Kerala state reference 1.5 M
Q2 How do children in Assam use bamboo bridges during the monsoon? What is a 'Jugaad' vehicle in Gujarat? Regional Transport • Bamboo Bridges & Jugaad 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Bamboo Bridges in Assam:
During the heavy monsoon in Assam, water often rises knee-deep or waist-deep on village roads. Children and villagers tie long, sturdy bamboo poles and ropes together across streams to create narrow, elevated footbridges. Children hold their books in one hand and grasp the bamboo railing with the other to cross safely.

2. The 'Jugaad' Vehicle in Gujarat:
A 'Jugaad' is an ingenious locally-assembled vehicle made by attaching the front engine and handlebar of a motorcycle or scooter to a wooden cart chassis with wheels at the back. It carries several children together to school, making a characteristic 'phut-phut-phut' sound.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Assam bamboo bridge construction and crossing technique 1.5 M
Gujarat Jugaad mechanical structure and purpose 1.5 M
Q3 What difficulties do children face while walking through thick jungles or deep snow to reach school? Terrain Adaptation • Jungles and Snow 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Walking Through Thick Jungles:
In dense forests, sunlight barely penetrates, creating darkness even during the day. The paths are overgrown with thorns, and children must stay alert to snake bites, insects, and wild animals, guiding themselves by listening to bird calls and animal sounds.

2. Walking on Snow (Northern Hills):
Children must hold hands carefully. If the snow is fresh and soft, their feet sink deep into it, making walking exhausting. If the snow is frozen hard, the surface becomes icy and dangerously slippery, causing children to slip and fall.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Jungle navigation risks and sensory awareness 1.5 M
Soft snow sinking vs frozen ice slipping hazards 1.5 M
Q4 How is a permanent cement bridge different from a temporary bamboo bridge? Which one is safer and why? Bridge Engineering • Cement vs Bamboo 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Comparison of Bridges:
• Cement Bridge: Made of strong baked bricks, cement, concrete, and iron rods. It is wide, has sturdy railings, can carry heavy vehicular loads, and lasts for decades safely.
• Bamboo Bridge: Made by tying long bamboo poles and ropes across streams. It is narrow, shaky, slippery during monsoon, and requires regular repairs.
• Verdict: A cement bridge is far safer and more durable.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Cement bridge materials and strength 1.5 M
Bamboo bridge fragility and safety contrast 1.5 M
Q5 What is a pulley? How does a pulley help in drawing water from a deep village well or sliding a trolley across a canyon? Simple Machines • The Pulley 3 Marks

The Pulley:
A pulley is a grooved wheel with a rope passing over it.
• Advantage: It changes the direction of pulling force. Instead of lifting a heavy load upwards against gravity, a person pulls the rope downwards using their own body weight, making lifting much easier and safer.

Camel in Desert:

• School Cart: In Rajasthan, sand dunes make walking exhausting. A camel cart pulls children comfortably across hot shifting sands to school.

Camel cart function for school children 1.5 M

Children sit together on a wooden cart pulled slowly by two bullocks through green village fields. On hot sunny afternoons or during rains, they hold colourful umbrellas overhead to protect themselves from the sun and downpours.
