Chapter 2: Ear to Ear

Animal Ears, Hearing Mechanisms, Skin Patterns & Mammals vs. Egg-Laying Animals

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Animals whose ears can be seen outside: Elephants (fan-like), rabbits (leaf-like on top of head), deer, dogs, cows.
  • Animals whose ears are hidden tiny holes covered with feathers: Birds (sparrows, crows, ducks), lizards, and crocodiles.
  • The Golden Rule of Animal Reproduction: Animals with visible external ears and hair on their body give birth to live babies (Mammals / Viviparous).
  • Animals without external ears and without hair (scales/feathers) lay eggs (Oviparous).
  • Skin patterns: Zebra stripes, tiger stripes, leopard rosettes, deer spots.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is the biological rule that tells us whether an animal gives birth to babies or lays eggs just by observing its ears and skin? Give two examples of each group. Biological Classification • Animal Science 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
The Golden Rule:
1. Animals that give birth to live babies (Viviparous / Mammals):
• Those animals whose ears can be seen outside on their heads AND who have hair or fur on their skin give birth to young babies.
• Examples: Cow, Dog, Elephant, Cat, Human beings.

2. Animals that lay eggs (Oviparous):
• Those animals whose ears cannot be seen from outside (they have tiny hidden ear holes covered by feathers or scales) AND who do not have hair on their skin lay eggs.
• Examples: Sparrow, Pigeon, Snake, Lizard, Crocodile, Frog.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Detailed rule for live-bearing animals (visible ears + hair) 1.5 M
Detailed rule for egg-laying animals (hidden ear holes + no hair) 1.5 M
Two accurate examples for each group 1.0 M
Q2 Name two animals whose ears look like fans and two whose ears are on top of their head. Why do animals have different patterns on their skin? Animal Morphology • Ears and Camouflage 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Ear Shapes:
• Fan-like Ears: Elephant (large fleshy flaps that flap to cool the body).
• Leaf-like Ears: Deer, Cow, Buffalo.
• Ears on Top of Head: Rabbit, Hare, Giraffe.

2. Skin Patterns:
The patterns (stripes on tigers and zebras, spots on leopards and deer) are due to the colors of the hair growing on their skin. These patterns provide camouflage, helping animals blend into shadows and grasses to hide from predators or sneak up on prey.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate animal examples for fan-like and top-of-head ears 1.5 M
Explanation of hair pigmentation and camouflage 1.5 M
Q3 How do snakes detect approaching humans or prey if they do not have external ears? Sensory Perception • Snakes and Birds 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Snakes' Hearing Mechanism:
Snakes do not have external ears, ear openings, or eardrums. Instead, they feel sound vibrations traveling through the ground. Their lower jawbone rests close to the earth and acts as a sensitive acoustic sensor, transmitting ground tremors directly to their inner ear bones.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific explanation of ground vibration detection via jawbone 2.0 M
Q4 Why can we see the external ears of dogs, cows, and elephants, but not the ears of birds, frogs, and lizards? External Ears • Mammals vs Non-Mammals 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
External Ears vs Hidden Holes:
• Mammals like dogs and elephants have prominent outer ear flaps (called pinnae) that collect sound waves.
• Birds, frogs, and lizards do not have external ear flaps. Instead, they have tiny ear openings on both sides of their heads covered and protected by feathers or thin skin membranes.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Mammalian pinnae explained 1.5 M
Hidden holes covered with feathers/skin 1.5 M
Q5 State the universal biological rule relating animal skin hair, external ears, and how they reproduce. Biological Rule • Hair and Birth 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Biological Rule:
1. Viviparous (Give Birth): Animals that have visible external ears and hair on their bodies give birth to live young ones (e.g., Cow, Cat, Human, Elephant).
2. Oviparous (Lay Eggs): Animals that do not have external ears and have feathers or scales instead of hair lay eggs (e.g., Birds, Snakes, Lizards, Crocodiles).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Rule for live-bearing animals (hair + external ears) 2 M
Rule for egg-laying animals (no hair + hidden ears) 2 M
Q6 How do birds hear faint sounds in the forest even though they lack outer ears? Avian Ears • Birds 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Bird Hearing:
Birds have tiny ear holes located just behind their eyes, shielded by specialized contour feathers that reduce wind noise while funneling subtle acoustic vibrations directly into their inner eardrums.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Position behind eyes and feather protection 1 M
Acoustic funneling to inner ear 1 M
Q7 Why do tigers, zebras, and leopards have stripes and spots on their skin and fur? Animal Camouflage • Skin Patterns 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Skin Patterns & Camouflage:
The distinct stripes of a tiger and spots of a leopard break up their visual outline in tall grass and forest shadows. This camouflage hides them from prey while stalking and protects young cubs from predators.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Breaking visual outline in grass/shadows 1.5 M
Predatory advantage and cub protection 1.5 M
Q8 Which animal is the National Animal of India? Why has its population decreased drastically, and what is 'Project Tiger'? National Animal • Royal Bengal Tiger 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
The Royal Bengal Tiger:
• National Animal: The Tiger.
• Decline: Illegal poaching for skin and bones, and deforestation destroying natural prey and habitats.
• Project Tiger: A nationwide conservation program launched by the Indian Government to establish dedicated tiger reserves and protect tigers from extinction.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Tiger identified as National Animal 1 M
Reasons for decline (poaching, deforestation) 1.5 M
Project Tiger conservation explained 1.5 M
Q9 What are dinosaurs? Which modern living reptiles resemble them, and why did dinosaurs disappear? Extinct Animals • Dinosaurs 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Dinosaurs:
Dinosaurs were giant prehistoric reptiles that lived millions of years ago. Modern lizards, crocodiles, and birds are their closest relatives. They became extinct due to massive asteroid impacts and catastrophic climate changes.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Prehistoric reptiles and living relatives 1 M
Asteroid/climate extinction cause 1 M

Lizard & Crocodile Ears:
Yes, on close observation, one can see two tiny dot-like holes on the sides of their head behind the eyes, which serve as their ears.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Tiny dot-like holes identified behind eyes 2 M
Q11 Classify the following animals into Egg-layers and Live-young bearers: Duck, Buffalo, Peacock, Bat, Frog, Whale. Classification • Oviparous vs Viviparous 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Classification:

Correct classification of all six animals 3 M
Q12 Why can animals like deer, dogs, and horses turn their external ears in different directions? Sensory Function • Ear Direction 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Movable Pinnae:
Animals have ear muscles that allow them to swivel their pinnae independently towards the source of a sound to pinpoint danger without turning their heads.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Independent ear rotation to locate predators 2 M

Every species plays a vital role in maintaining the ecological food web. The Wildlife Protection Act bans hunting to prevent extinction, preserve biodiversity, and safeguard national heritage.

Crocodile and Lizard Hearing Mechanism

Real-World Environment Context: A student observes a garden lizard on a wall and wonders if lizards are deaf because she cannot see any external ear flaps.

Analytical Task: Are lizards and crocodiles deaf? Explain how they hear sounds.

No, lizards and crocodiles are not deaf; they have keen hearing. Instead of external fleshy ear flaps (pinnae), they have tiny, sensitive ear holes on either side of their head behind their eyes. These ear canals are protected by thin scales or membrane folds that capture acoustic vibrations accurately.

Chapter 3: A Day with Nandu

Baby Elephant Nandu, Elephant Herd Dynamics, Matriarchal Leadership & Wildlife Facts

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Nandu: A three-month-old baby elephant weighing 200 kilograms.
  • An adult elephant can eat more than 100 kilograms of green leaves and twigs in a single day.
  • Elephants sleep for only 2 to 4 hours in a day; mud and water keep their thick skin cool; large fan-like ears flap to release body heat.
  • Herd structure: An elephant herd has only female elephants and their young calves. The oldest female is the Matriarch (leader) of the herd.
  • Male elephants stay in the herd only until they are 14 to 15 years old, then leave to wander alone.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 Who is the leader of an elephant herd? What role do male elephants play in the herd, and why do elephants love playing in mud and water? Wildlife Biology • Elephant Herd Structure 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Leader of the Herd:
The oldest female elephant (the Matriarch / Nani ma) is the supreme leader of the herd. She decides when to move, finds waterholes during droughts, and directs the herd's defense.

2. Role of Male Elephants:
Male elephant calves live in the herd only until they are 14 to 15 years old. Once they reach maturity, they leave the herd to wander and forage independently alone in the forest.

3. Why Elephants Love Mud and Water:
Elephants do not have sweat glands across their thick skin. Rolling in cool mud coats their skin with a protective layer that shields them from scorching tropical sun and insect bites. Splashing water and flapping their giant ears acts like a natural air conditioner, cooling the blood vessels running through the ear flaps.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identifies oldest female (matriarch) as leader 1.0 M
Explains male calves leaving at age 14-15 1.5 M
Scientific cooling function of mud coating and ear flapping 1.5 M
Q2 Who is the leader of an elephant herd? Why do male elephants leave the herd when they grow up? Wildlife Ecology • Elephant Herd Behavior 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Leader of the Herd:
The oldest female elephant is the Matriarch (leader) of the herd. She decides when to move, where to find waterholes, and protects the young calves.

2. Why Male Elephants Leave:
An elephant herd consists exclusively of female elephants and their babies. Young male calves live in the herd only until they reach 14 to 15 years of age. Once they mature, they leave the maternal herd to live independently or form small bachelor groups.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Matriarch role and duties explained 1.5 M
Male elephants leaving at age 14-15 explained 1.5 M
Q3 How does the life of an elephant in a wild forest differ from that of an elephant tied in chains in a circus? Animal Welfare • Freedom vs. Captivity 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Wild vs. Captive Elephant:
• In the Wild: Elephants roam freely across vast jungle corridors, bathe in natural rivers, feed on fresh bamboo and grasses, play socially with herd members, and express natural maternal instincts.
• In Captivity: Captive elephants are often tied with heavy metal chains on concrete floors, kept in solitary isolation, beaten with bullhooks (ankush) to perform unnatural circus tricks, and deprived of natural foraging and social herds.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three natural conditions in the wild described 1.5 M
Cruelty and confinement in captivity contrasted 1.5 M

Animal Empathy and Captivity Ethics

Real-World Environment Context: Circuses and tourist sites keep elephants tied tightly with iron chains on concrete floors, forcing them to carry heavy tourist howdahs.

Analytical Task: Based on 'A Day with Nandu', why is chaining an elephant deeply cruel, and how does it violate their natural social life?

Elephants are highly intelligent, emotional, and social beings who thrive by walking up to 20 km daily in cooperative family herds. Solitary confinement with heavy iron chains causes severe joint arthritis, psychological trauma, and deprives them of essential mud baths and family bonding.

Chapter 4: The Story of Amrita

Bishnoi Community of Khejadli Village (Rajasthan), Khejadi Trees & Ultimate Sacrifice

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Historical event from Khejadli village near Jodhpur, Rajasthan, over 300 years ago.
  • The Bishnoi principle: 'Agar pedh hain toh hum hain' (If trees survive, so do we).
  • Amrita Devi and her daughters hugging the sacred Khejadi trees to prevent the King's soldiers from axing them for palace timber.
  • Over 363 Bishnois sacrificed their lives protecting the forest; the King was deeply moved, issued a royal decree banning tree felling and animal hunting in Bishnoi lands forever.
  • Adaptations of the Khejadi tree: Needs very little water in deserts, bark used for medicine, beans (sangri) eaten as vegetables.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why did the King of Jodhpur want to cut the trees of Khejadli village? How did Amrita and the Bishnoi villagers react, and what was the King's final decree? Environmental History & Indigenous Wisdom 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why the King wanted timber:
The Maharaja of Jodhpur wanted to build a new palace and ordered his soldiers to fell Khejadi trees from Khejadli village to burn lime and produce timber for the palace construction.

2. The Bishnoi Resistance:
The Bishnois considered Khejadi trees sacred members of their family. Amrita Devi hugged a tree trunk tightly, refusing to move. When the soldiers mercilessly chopped down the trees, Amrita, her three young daughters, and over 360 villagers laid down their lives embracing the trees.

3. The King's Final Decree:
When the King heard of this unprecedented sacrifice, he was filled with remorse and respect. He personally visited the village and issued a royal copper-plate decree: No green tree would ever be cut and no animal would ever be hunted in Bishnoi territory. Even today, Bishnoi villages are flourishing green oases where blackbucks, chinkaras, and peacocks roam fearlessly.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
King's palace construction motive 1.0 M
Amrita Devi and 363 villagers tree-hugging sacrifice 1.5 M
Royal decree banning logging and hunting permanently 1.5 M
Q2 Describe the unique characteristics of the Khejadi tree that make it so vital to the people of the Thar Desert. Botanical Features • The Khejadi Tree 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Unique Characteristics of the Khejadi Tree:
1. Low Water Requirement: It grows abundantly in harsh desert areas with minimal rainfall.
2. Medicinal Bark: Its bark is used by locals to prepare herbal medicines for coughs and skin diseases.
3. Edible Pods (Sangri): People harvest and cook its nutritious green beans (sangri) as a staple vegetable.
4. Shade & Fodder: Children play under its wide, dense shade, and desert animals (like goats and blackbucks) eat its protein-rich leaves.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Four distinct practical features of the Khejadi tree 3.0 M
Q3 Who are the Bishnois of Rajasthan? What pledge did they take to protect trees and wildlife? Environmental Movements • The Bishnois 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. The Bishnoi Community:
The Bishnois are a dedicated nature-loving community living in Rajasthan who follow 29 environmental principles laid down by Guru Jambheshwar in the 15th century.

2. Sacred Environmental Pledge:
They consider all trees (especially Khejadi) and animals (like blackbucks, chinkaras, and peacocks) sacred. They protect forests with their lives, strictly forbid hunting, and ensure animals roam fearlessly around their villages.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

Real-World Environment Context: The Khejadi tree flourishes in the dry Thar Desert where very little water is available.

Chapter 5: Anita and the Honeybees

True Story of Girl Star Anita Khushwaha (Muzaffarpur, Bihar), Apiculture & Education

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Anita Khushwaha of Bochaha village in Muzaffarpur district, Bihar: Overcoming poverty and orthodox barriers to attend school.
  • Teaching younger children to earn money for her own college education.
  • Apiculture (Beekeeping): Learning to keep bees in litchi orchards. Litchi flowers bloom in February, attracting honeybees.
  • Bee boxes: Cost ₹2,000 per box (sugar syrup for food, medicine for cleaning hives). Each box produces 12 kg of honey.
  • Hierarchy in a beehive: One Queen Bee (lays eggs), Worker Bees (majority; fly miles to collect nectar, make honey, care for larvae), and Male Drone Bees.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 Describe the division of labor inside a honeybee hive. What are the three types of bees and their respective duties? Social Empowerment & Apiculture Biology 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
A beehive functions with extraordinary cooperation and strict division of labor:
1. The Queen Bee: There is only one fertile Queen Bee in each hive. Her sole duty is to lay thousands of eggs daily to maintain the colony.
2. Worker Bees (Female): They make up 95% of the hive population. They perform all the arduous work: flying miles across orchards to collect sweet nectar from flowers, fanning nectar into honey, feeding young larvae, building wax honeycombs, and guarding the entrance against intruders.
3. Male Bees (Drones): They are few in number and do not gather food or work inside the hive; their only role is mating with the queen.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Role of Queen Bee (laying eggs) 1.0 M
Role of Worker Bees (nectar collection, comb building, hive care) 1.5 M
Role of Male Drone Bees 0.5 M
Q2 Describe the three types of honeybees found in a beehive and the specific duties performed by each. Insect Sociology • Honeybee Colony 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Three Types of Bees in a Hive:
1. The Queen Bee: The largest bee in the colony. Her sole duty is to lay thousands of eggs daily to maintain the colony population.
2. Worker Bees: Female bees that perform all hard labour—building the wax honeycomb cells, cleaning the hive, flying out to collect nectar and pollen from flowers, nursing young larvae, and guarding the hive entrance.
3. Male Bees (Drones): They have no stinger and do not collect nectar. Their primary role is to mate with the queen.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Queen bee role described correctly 1.5 M
Worker bee duties detailed 1.5 M
Drone role defined 1.0 M
Q3 How does a worker honeybee communicate to other bees when she discovers a rich flower patch? Communication in Nature • The Bee Dance 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
The Bee Dance (Waggle Dance):
When a scout bee discovers flowers laden with sweet nectar, she returns to the hive and performs a special rhythmic circular and figure-eight dance (the waggle dance). The speed, angle, and vibration of the dance communicate the exact direction relative to the Sun and the distance of the nectar source to all other worker bees.

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

The 'Right to Education' (RTE Act)

Real-World Environment Context: Anita's parents initially thought educating a girl was a waste of money because they had to buy uniforms and books.

Analytical Task: How does the Right to Education (RTE) Act guarantee that every child from Class 1 to 8 can study for free?

The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act guarantees that all children between 6 and 14 years have the fundamental right to free education in government schools without paying any tuition fees. Uniforms, textbooks, and hot mid-day meals are provided by the government so no child is denied schooling due to poverty.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for explaining RTE Act (ages 6-14, zero tuition fee); 1.5 Marks for uniforms, books, and mid-day meal provision.

Chapter 6: Omana's Journey

Train Travel from Ahmedabad to Kerala, Railway Stations, Platforms & Ticket Checkers (TTE)

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Omana's diary format: Traveling from Gujarat to Kerala with family.
  • Railway platform observations: Coolies (porters in red uniforms with brass badges), snack stalls (dhokla, lemon rice, chai), luggage weighing.
  • The role of the Travelling Ticket Examiner (TTE): Checking reservation charts, seat numbers, and validating photo tickets.
  • Train accommodations: Berths (Lower, Middle, Upper, Side Lower, Side Upper), windows with iron bars, emergency brakes.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 How can you identify a Travelling Ticket Examiner (TTE) in a train coach? What three tasks does a TTE perform? Railway Systems & Public Etiquette 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Identification of a TTE:
A TTE wears a crisp black coat with an official Indian Railways brass nameplate badge pinned on the lapel, white shirt, grey or black trousers, and carries the official paper reservation chart or a digital handheld terminal (HHT tablet).

Three Tasks Performed by a TTE:
1. Checking Tickets: Verifies that passengers hold valid reserved tickets for the correct date, train, coach, and berth.
2. Checking Photo IDs: Confirms the passenger's identity using Aadhaar or school cards.
3. Allotting Vacant Berths: Checks for absentees and allots vacant seats to waitlisted (RAC/WL) passengers transparently.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Visual identification (black coat, badge, chart) 1.5 M
Three duties (validating tickets, ID verification, vacant berth allotment) 1.5 M
Q2 List four community helpers or facilities you observe on a busy railway platform during a journey. Railway Operations • The Platform 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Facilities and Helpers on a Railway Platform:
1. Porters (Coolies): Wearing red shirts and brass arm badges, they carry heavy passenger luggage on their heads safely to the coach.
2. Ticket Checker (TTE): Checks passengers' reserved tickets against the reservation chart to ensure everyone is on their allotted berth.
3. Station Master & Signal Staff: Manage train arrivals, departures, track switching, and safety flags.
4. Public Announcement System & Water Kiosks: Announce train arrival times, platform numbers, and provide filtered drinking water.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Four helpers/facilities correctly identified with duties 3.0 M
Q3 What civic rules should passengers follow while traveling on long-distance trains? Civic Etiquette • Train Travel 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Rules for Responsible Train Travel:
• Never pull the emergency chain without a genuine life-safety emergency.
• Do not litter food packets or plastic cups on tracks; deposit all waste in coach dustbins.
• Avoid speaking loudly or playing mobile speakers at night so co-passengers can sleep peacefully.
• Keep toilets clean and flush after every use.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Cleanliness on Railway Tracks

Real-World Environment Context: Some passengers throw empty plastic tea cups and banana peels out of train windows while moving.

Analytical Task: Why is throwing trash out of train windows dangerous, and what proper method should passengers use?

Litter flying out at 90 km/h can hit track maintenance workers (gangmen) or shatter nearby glass. Plastic waste chokes track drainage and harms wild animals along forest tracks. Passengers must deposit all wrappers in the coach dustbin located near the toilets or hand them to the onboard cleaning staff.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for hazards to workers, environment, and wildlife; 1.5 Marks for using onboard coach dustbins.

Chapter 7: From the Window

Changing Landscapes: Red Soil of Goa, Konkan Railway Bridges, Tunnels & Level Crossings

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The Konkan Railway journey: Rolling past green paddy fields, coconut groves, and reddish laterite soil of Goa.
  • The sheer engineering feat of the Konkan route: 2,000 bridges and 92 tunnels carved through the Western Ghats (Sahyadri mountains).
  • Level crossings: Understanding safety barriers, waiting for the train to pass, and turning off vehicle engines to save fuel.
  • Crossing the massive bridge over the Zuari/Mandovi river: Hearing the hollow, echoing sound of train wheels on open steel bridge girders.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why did the sound of the train wheels change dramatically when crossing the long river bridge? How many tunnels and bridges exist on the route from Goa to Kerala? Railway Geography & Sound Physics 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why the wheel sound changed:
When running over ordinary ground, sound waves bounce off the solid earthen embankment and ballast stones. But when the train moved onto the steel river bridge, there was no solid ground under the tracks—only open steel girders and deep river water below. The steel metal reverberated, creating a loud, hollow, echoing 'khad-khad-khad' rumbling roar.

2. Engineering statistics:
Along the scenic Western Ghats route from Goa to Kerala, the train passes through 92 mountain tunnels and crosses 2,000 river and ravine bridges.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Hollow echoing sound physics of open steel girders over water 1.5 M
Exact statistics: 92 tunnels and 2,000 bridges 1.5 M
Q2 Why are there 2000 bridges and 92 tunnels on the Konkan Railway route between Goa and Kerala? Railway Engineering • Bridges and Tunnels 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Reasons for Numerous Bridges and Tunnels:
The Konkan Railway traverses the rugged, magnificent Western Ghats mountain range and coastal river systems. The train route must cross numerous deep river estuaries, backwater creeks, and gorges (requiring 2000 bridges) and pierce through solid granite mountain ridges (requiring 92 excavated tunnels) to maintain a smooth, level track without steep gradients.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Geographical topography of Western Ghats and rivers 1.5 M
Engineering necessity of bridges and tunnels explained 1.5 M
Q3 Why is it dangerous to cross a railway track under a closed level crossing barrier? What precautions must drivers take? Road Safety • Level Crossings 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Danger of Crossing Under Closed Gates:
Level crossing gates are closed when a high-speed express train is approaching. Modern trains travel at over 100 km/h and take hundreds of metres to stop even after braking. Crossing under the gate can lead to fatal collisions.

2. Precautions:
Drivers and pedestrians must wait patiently behind the white stop line, switch off vehicle engines to save fuel and reduce noise, and proceed only after the barrier is fully raised.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Speed of trains and fatal collision danger 1.0 M
Turning off engines and waiting behind line 1.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Fuel Conservation at Railway Level Crossings

Real-World Environment Context: At a closed railway crossing gate, dozens of motorists keep their car, bus, and scooter engines idling, filling the air with thick smoke and deafening horn noise.

Analytical Task: Why should motorists switch off vehicle engines while waiting at a closed railway gate?

A railway gate remains closed for 5 to 10 minutes. Turning off engines saves costly petrol and diesel, cuts carbon emissions, prevents air pollution from choking waiting pedestrians, and eliminates unbearable noise, making the environment cleaner.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for fuel savings and emission reduction; 1.5 Marks for air and noise pollution prevention.

Chapter 8: Reaching Grandmother's House

Kerala Backwaters, Ferry Boats, Valyamma's House & Reading Railway Timetables

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Arriving at Kottayam station; traveling to Valyamma's (mother's elder sister) house in an auto-rickshaw.
  • The Ferry Boat ride: People, bicycles, cows, and coconuts boarding the public ferry to cross the river to Ammuma's (grandmother's) village island.
  • Reading railway timetables: Train number, station name, arrival time, departure time, distance in kilometers, day of journey.
  • Cost of tickets and appreciating water transportation networks.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is a 'ferry'? What information can you learn by reading a train timetable like the 16347 Express? Timetable Analysis & Travel Logistics 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. What is a Ferry:
A ferry is a flat-bottomed passenger boat used to carry people, vehicles, and goods across a river, canal, or lagoon where there is no permanent bridge.

2. Information from a Railway Timetable:
A train timetable provides comprehensive journey data:
• Station names in the exact sequence of the journey.
• Scheduled Arrival Time and Departure Time at each halt.
• Total Distance in kilometres from the starting station.
• The day of the journey (Day 1, Day 2).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Definition and purpose of public ferry 1.0 M
Lists 4 specific data points from railway timetables 2.0 M
Q2 What important details are printed on an Indian Railways train ticket? Mention any four. Information Literacy • Reading a Train Ticket 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Key Details on a Train Ticket:
1. PNR Number (Passenger Name Record): A unique 10-digit booking reference code.
2. Train Number & Name: Identifies the specific express train.
3. Date of Journey & Departure Time: Exact day and scheduled boarding time.
4. Coach & Berth Number: (e.g., Coach B1, Berth 24 - Lower).
5. Distance & Total Fare: Distance traveled in kilometres and ticket cost in rupees.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Four accurate pieces of information printed on train tickets 3.0 M
Q3 How does a ferry boat operate in the backwaters of Kerala? Why is it a lifeline for local villagers? Water Transport • Ferry Services 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Ferry Boats in Kerala:
In Kerala's water-locked backwater regions (like Alappuzha and Kottayam), islands are separated by wide lagoons and canals with no road bridges. Sturdy passenger ferry boats operate continuously like water-buses, transporting villagers, office workers, vegetables, bicycles, and schoolchildren safely across waterways for a nominal fare.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Role of ferry as public water transit in canal geography 2.0 M

Chapter 10: Hu Tu Tu, Hu Tu Tu

The Sport of Kabaddi, Physical Stamina, Rules & The Inspiring Story of Karnam Malleswari

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The game of Kabaddi: Holding breath while chanting 'Kabaddi-Kabaddi', tagging opponents, crossing the central midline safely.
  • Physical coordination: Sharp reflexes, lung stamina, leg sweeps, and team catching.
  • Olympic Inspiration: Karnam Malleswari, weightlifter from Andhra Pradesh, daughter of a police constable. Started lifting at age 12; won India's first Olympic bronze medal in weightlifting at Sydney 2000 (can lift 130 kg!).
  • Sisters Jwala, Leela, and Heera: Pioneering women who broke taboos to play and coach Kabaddi in Mumbai 50 years ago.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 What are the essential rules of Kabaddi? Who is Karnam Malleswari, and what historic achievement did she accomplish for Indian sports? Sports Rules & Women in Sports 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Essential Rules of Kabaddi:
• A raider crosses the center line into the opposing team's court while chanting 'Kabaddi-Kabaddi' continuously in a single breath without stopping.
• The raider tries to touch one or more defending players and rush back safely across the midline.
• If defenders pin the raider down until they lose their breath, the raider is declared 'Out'. If the raider touches the center line, all touched defenders are 'Out'.

2. Karnam Malleswari's Historic Achievement:
Karnam Malleswari is an internationally celebrated weightlifter from Andhra Pradesh. Daughter of a police constable, she began training at age 12. At the Sydney 2000 Olympic Games, she won a Bronze Medal, becoming the first Indian woman in history to win an Olympic medal. She has won 29 international medals and can lift up to 130 kg.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurately details raider chant, breath control, and tag-out rules 2.0 M
Highlights Karnam Malleswari as first Indian woman Olympic medalist 2.0 M
Q2 Who is Karnam Malleswari? Summarize her athletic achievements in Indian sports history. Sports Excellence • Karnam Malleswari 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Karnam Malleswari:
Karnam Malleswari is an iconic Indian weightlifter from Andhra Pradesh. She started weightlifting at the age of 12 under her coach's guidance.

Major Achievements:
• She became capable of lifting a massive weight of 130 kilograms.
• At the 2000 Sydney Olympic Games, she made history by becoming the first Indian woman ever to win an Olympic medal (Bronze in 69 kg category).
• She has won 29 international medals in world weightlifting championships, inspiring millions of Indian girls to take up competitive sports.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Identification as pioneer Olympic weightlifter from AP 1.5 M
Sydney 2000 Olympic bronze and 130 kg lifting record 1.5 M
Q3 Who were the three sisters Jwala, Leela, and Heera? How did they overcome conservative social norms to promote Kabaddi? Inspiring Women • The Kabaddi Sisters 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
The Kabaddi Sisters (Jwala, Leela, Heera):
Living in Mumbai more than fifty years ago, these three sisters loved playing Kabaddi. In those times, society believed girls should not play aggressive games wearing shorts, fearing nobody would marry them.

Their Courage:
Supported by their open-minded mother and maternal uncles, they practiced determinedly, formed their own Kabaddi club, competed at national tournaments, and proved that women can excel in traditional contact sports with discipline and dignity.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Societal prejudices against women playing Kabaddi 1.5 M
Formation of club and national competitive success 1.5 M

Chapter 11: The Valley of Flowers

Chamoli, Uttarakhand, Floral Diversity, Madhubani Painting & Itr Making in Kannauj

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The Valley of Flowers: A breathtaking high-altitude national park nestled in the Chamoli district of Uttarakhand.
  • Blooming season: Flowers bloom for only a few brief weeks between July and September.
  • Madhubani folk art (Mithila, Bihar): Traditional wall paintings made with ground rice paste, indigo, turmeric, and flower dyes.
  • Kannauj (Uttar Pradesh): The perfume capital of India, renowned for manufacturing pure rose and jasmine 'Itr' (attar) using traditional deg-bhapka steam distillation.
  • Culinary flowers: Kachnar flower curry (UP), banana flower dishes (Kerala), and sahjan (drumstick) flower pakoras (Maharashtra).
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 Where is the Valley of Flowers located? What is 'Madhubani Painting', and what natural colors are used to make it? Geographical Heritage & Traditional Arts 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Location of Valley of Flowers:
The Valley of Flowers is a scenic national park situated in the high Himalayan hills of Chamoli district in Uttarakhand. It is blanketed with hundreds of vibrant flower species that bloom for a few short weeks after monsoon rains.

2. Madhubani Painting:
Madhubani is an ancient folk art form originating from the Mithila region of Bihar. During festivals and weddings, women paint courtyard walls and floors with pictures of human beings, animals, birds (peacocks), trees, and flowers.

3. Natural Colors Used:
The base paint is made of paste of powdered rice mixed with natural colors: blue from indigo (neel), yellow from turmeric (haldi), and various shades from tree bark and flowers.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Exact location in Chamoli, Uttarakhand 1.0 M
Madhubani origin in Mithila, Bihar 1.5 M
Use of powdered rice paste and natural plant dyes (indigo, haldi) 1.5 M
Q2 Describe the Madhubani art form of Bihar. What natural ingredients and subjects are used in these paintings? Traditional Folk Art • Madhubani Painting 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Madhubani Folk Art:
Madhubani (Mithila) is an ancient traditional folk art from Bihar, created during festivals, weddings, and celebrations.

2. Materials & Ingredients:
• The base paint paste is made of finely ground powdered rice mixed with water.
• Natural colours are extracted from plants: yellow from turmeric (haldi), blue from indigo (neel), green from leaves, and black from lamp soot.

3. Subjects Depicted:
Paintings feature human figures, birds (peacocks, parrots), fish, turtles, trees, flowers, and holy deities, filled with intricate geometric cross-hatch lines.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Geographical origin in Bihar and powdered rice paste base 1.5 M
Natural pigments and typical subjects detailed 1.5 M
Q3 Why is Kannauj in Uttar Pradesh world-famous? How is traditional 'Itr' (attar) prepared there? Commercial Botany • Kannauj Perfumes 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Kannauj - The Perfume Capital:
Kannauj is famous as the 'Itr City' of India. For centuries, entire generations of master distillers have manufactured pure, alcohol-free essential floral scents.

2. Preparation of Itr:
Truckloads of fresh rose petals (damask roses), jasmine, and kewra flowers are packed into large copper stills (degs). Water is added, the lid is sealed with mud, and heated over wood fires. Vapours condense through bamboo pipes (chonga) into receiver pots submerged in cold water, creating pure natural perfume.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Kannauj's heritage as Itr manufacturing hub 1.5 M
Deg-Bhapka hydro-distillation method explained 1.5 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Kannauj Traditional Itr Distillation

Real-World Environment Context: Truckloads of fresh damask roses arrive at Kannauj distilleries at 4:00 am every morning during harvest.

Analytical Task: How is traditional Kannauj 'Itr' made, and why is it superior to chemical alcohol perfumes?

Kannauj artisans use the centuries-old Deg-Bhapka hydro-distillation method. Fresh rose petals and water are boiled in sealed copper cauldrons (Degs); the fragrant steam passes through bamboo pipes into a receiver (Bhapka) immersed in cold water, condensing into pure sandalwood oil base. Unlike chemical synthetic sprays containing alcohol, pure Itr is 100% natural, therapeutic, and long-lasting.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for copper cauldron hydro-distillation; 1.5 Marks for natural purity vs chemical alcohol.

Chapter 12: Changing Times

Chetandas's Story: Partition of 1947, Sohna (Haryana), House Evolution & Modern Materials

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Partition of India (1947): Millions migrating; Chetandas moving from Dera Ghazi Khan (now Pakistan) to Delhi tents, then to Sohna, Haryana.
  • Evolution of housing materials over 60 years:
  • 1. First Mud House: Mud mixed with husk for walls; neem/keekar branches on roofs to prevent termites; cow dung coating on floors to keep insects away.
  • 2. Second Upgrade: Baked red bricks for walls, unbaked brick ceilings.
  • 3. Modern Times: Reinforced concrete (RBC/RCC), iron bars, cement, ceramic bathroom tiles, and modern flush sanitation.
  • Social progress: Elimination of manual scavenging; modern indoor plumbing.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why did Chetandas's mother coat the mud floor with cow dung mixed with earth? How did roofing materials change from his childhood to his grandchildren's generation? Social History & Building Materials 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why cow dung was coated on mud floors:
A mixture of fresh cow dung and clay is an age-old Indian biocidal technique. When dried, it creates a hard, dust-free floor surface that acts as a natural insect repellent, keeping termites, ants, and pests away from the mud walls.

2. Evolution of Roofing Materials:
• Childhood (1947): Roofs were made of wooden frames covered with keekar and neem branches (to prevent wood termites) overlaid with dried reed grass and mud.
• Youth (1970): Roofs upgraded to unbaked brick arches and steel girders.
• Grandchildren's Era: Modern roofs are made of durable RCC (Reinforced Cement Concrete) using steel iron rebar mesh, gravel, and cement, capable of supporting multi-story floors.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Scientific pest-repellent function of cow dung coating 1.5 M
Detailed 3-stage progression of roofing materials (thatch ➔ brick girders ➔ RCC) 2.5 M
Q2 How did the building materials in Chetandas' house change over three generations? Historical Architecture • Evolution of Materials 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Evolution of Building Materials:
1. First House (Partition Era): Mud walls coated with husk and cow-dung paste (to keep insects away) with neem/keekar wooden rafters and thatched roofs.
2. Second Generation: Sun-dried and unbaked clay bricks with iron girders and cement plaster.
3. Third Generation (Modern): Baked clay bricks, steel reinforced cement concrete (RCC), glazed tiles, marble flooring, and modern indoor PVC plumbing.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Clear three-stage material progression (mud -> brick -> RCC/tiles) 3.0 M
Q3 How were toilets built in Chetandas' first house, and how has modern indoor sanitation improved human dignity? Sanitation Systems • Dry vs. Modern Toilets 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Traditional Toilets:
In early days, people used open fields or a separate dry latrine behind the house where human waste collected in pans and had to be manually cleared by cleaners.

2. Modern Indoor Sanitation:
Modern homes have ceramic flush toilets with water seals connected to underground sewage pipes or septic tanks. Waste flushes away cleanly with water, ending the inhumane practice of manual scavenging and ensuring high hygiene and human dignity.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Contrast between manual dry latrine and modern flush toilet 2.0 M

Eliminating Manual Scavenging

Real-World Environment Context: In older times, dry latrines were built outside the house and people from specific marginalized castes were forced to clean human waste manually.

Analytical Task: How has modern septic tank and piped sewer plumbing restored human dignity and equality?

Manual scavenging was an inhuman, discriminatory practice. Modern water-sealed pour-flush toilets and underground sewer networks automate waste disposal sanitarily, ensuring nobody is forced to handle human excreta and guaranteeing human dignity, cleanliness, and social justice.

Chapter 13: A River's Tale

The Life Journey of a River: Mountain Purity, Human Pollution & Aquatic Conservation

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The stages of a river: Originates pristine and pure from melting Himalayan glaciers with abundant fish.
  • Passing through villages: People wash clothes, bathe cattle, and throw garbage; water clarity declines.
  • Passing through industrial cities: Factories dump untreated toxic chemicals, industrial effluents, and city sewage; water turns black and foul-smelling; fish die of oxygen starvation.
  • Water solubility: Substances that dissolve in water (sugar, salt, lemon juice) vs. substances that do not dissolve (oil, sand, plastic, chalk).
  • Purification methods: Boiling, alum (fitkari) sedimentation, chlorination, and solar treatment.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why does the color of a river change from crystal blue in the mountains to dark murky brown or black in industrial cities? Why do fish die in polluted river stretches? Environmental Science • Water Pollution 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why River Color Changes:
In high mountains, the river originates from clean glacial meltwater, free from human contamination. But as it flows past cities, municipal drains discharge millions of litres of untreated black toilet sewage, while factories dump toxic dyes, heavy metals, and chemical acids. This sludge turns the river dark, foul-smelling, and poisonous.

2. Why Fish Die:
Decomposing sewage and chemical waste consume all the dissolved oxygen present in water. Without adequate dissolved oxygen, aquatic organisms suffocate and die. Toxic factory chemicals also directly poison the fish's gills.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Contrasts glacial purity with industrial effluents and municipal sewage 1.5 M
Scientific explanation of dissolved oxygen depletion causing fish suffocation 1.5 M
Q2 List four major human activities that pollute clean rivers as they flow through cities and industrial towns. Environmental Pollution • River Ecosystems 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Four Major Causes of River Pollution:
1. Untreated Industrial Effluents: Factories dumping toxic chemicals, heavy metals, and dyes directly into river streams.
2. Municipal Sewage: City drains discharging millions of litres of untreated domestic blackwater and bathroom waste.
3. Agricultural Runoff: Chemical fertilizers and poisonous pesticides washed into rivers during heavy rains.
4. Religious & Domestic Immersion: Washing clothes with harsh detergents, bathing cattle, and immersing non-biodegradable painted idols.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Four distinct, scientifically accurate pollution sources 3.0 M
Q3 Explain how dirty muddy water can be purified at home for drinking during flood emergencies. Water Purification • Domestic Methods 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Emergency Water Purification Steps:
1. Sedimentation & Decantation: Let muddy water sit undisturbed in a bucket. Heavy mud settles to the bottom; pour the clearer water into another vessel.
2. Alum (Fitkari) Swirling: Swirl a small piece of alum in water to rapidly coagulate fine suspended clay particles.
3. Filtration & Boiling: Strain through a clean multi-layered cotton cloth, then boil vigorously for 10–15 minutes to kill all pathogenic germs.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three logical steps: sedimentation, alum treatment, boiling 3.0 M

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Soluble vs Insoluble Kitchen Substances

Real-World Environment Context: A student tests six substances in glasses of water: Sugar, Cooking Oil, Salt, Chalk Powder, Turmeric, and Sand.

Analytical Task: Classify these six items into: (a) Completely Soluble in water, (b) Insoluble in water.

(a) Completely Soluble: Sugar, Salt (they dissolve completely and disappear into the water).
(b) Insoluble: Cooking Oil (floats on top), Chalk Powder (settles down), Turmeric (leaves sediment), Sand (sinks to the bottom).
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for correctly identifying soluble pair; 1.5 Marks for four insoluble items.

Chapter 14: Basva's Farm

Onion Cultivation in Belagavi (Karnataka), Farming Tools & Timely Harvesting

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Traditional agriculture in Belagavi, Karnataka: The complete onion crop cycle.
  • Traditional agricultural implements:
  • 1. Khunti: An iron rod used to dig and loosen hard soil before sowing.
  • 2. Kurige: A wooden bullock-drawn plough with a seed funnel for dropping seeds at equal distance and depth.
  • 3. Illige: A sharp curved blade fixed to a wooden block used to slice dry leaves from onions.
  • The threat of weeds (kharpatwar): Unwanted wild plants that consume water and fertilizer meant for crops; must be weeded out early.
  • Timely harvesting: Onions must be dug out immediately once green leaves turn yellow and dry; delayed harvest rots the crop in wet soil.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is the function of the 'Khunti', 'Kurige', and 'Illige' in onion farming? What are weeds, and why must they be removed from crops? Agricultural Implements & Techniques 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Agricultural Implements:
• Khunti: An iron rod used to dig and soften the soil before ploughing so seeds can sprout easily.
• Kurige: A wooden plough drawn by bullocks with a funnel. Seeds are dropped into the funnel and sown at regular distances and depths.
• Illige: A curved sharp sickle fixed on a wooden base. Basva's mother sits on the block and uses the blade to slice dried leaves from harvested onions.

2. Weeds (Kharpatwar) and Removal:
Weeds are unwanted wild plants that grow naturally in fields alongside cultivated crops. They steal water, sunlight, and soil nutrients (fertilizers) meant for the crop, stunting onion growth. Therefore, weeds must be uprooted early.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Detailed function of Khunti, Kurige, and Illige 2.5 M
Definition of weeds and damage caused to crops 1.5 M
Q2 Name the traditional agricultural implements used in Basva's onion farm in Karnataka and explain the function of each. Agricultural Implements • Tools of Karnataka 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Implements Used in Basva's Farm:
1. Khunti: An iron rod used by Basva's father to dig and loosen the hard soil before sowing so roots can penetrate easily.
2. Kurige: A traditional seed drill tied behind bullocks. As bullocks walk, seeds drop through a funnel-like pipe at regular depth and spacing.
3. Illige: A curved, sharp sickle blade fixed to a wooden base. Basva's mother sits on it and uses both hands to slice off dried onion leaves from bulbs.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three tools correctly named (Khunti, Kurige, Illige) 1.5 M
Accurate function of each implement 1.5 M
Q3 Why must weeds be pulled out of onion fields? Why is timely harvesting crucial for an onion crop? Crop Management • Weeding & Harvesting 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Need for Weeding:
Weeds are unwanted wild plants that grow naturally alongside crops. If not removed, they steal water, fertilizers, and sunlight meant for onion plants, resulting in stunted, tiny bulbs.

2. Timely Harvesting:
When onion leaves turn yellow and dry, the bulbs are mature. If harvesting is delayed even a few days, onions rot under wet soil and the farmer's entire hard work is ruined.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Weed competition for nutrients explained 1.5 M
Consequences of delayed harvesting (rotting) 1.5 M

Risk of Delayed Onion Harvesting

Real-World Environment Context: Basva's father warns the family: 'All of us must work together to dig out the onions right now. If we delay even by a few days, the entire crop will be ruined.'

Analytical Task: Why does a delay in harvesting cause onions to rot underground?

When onion leaves turn yellow and dry, the underground bulb is fully mature. If it is not dug out promptly, late rains or soil moisture will cause the mature bulbs to rot in the mud or sprout green shoots again, destroying their shelf life and rendering them unsellable.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for mature bulb state; 1.5 Marks for moisture rotting and premature resprouting.

Chapter 15: From Market to Home

Vaishali's Family, Vegetable Vendor's Strenuous Routine, Perishable vs Long-Lasting Produce

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Vaishali's father (Babuji) is a vegetable vendor in Delhi; the family's rigorous daily schedule begins at 3:00 am.
  • Sorting previous day's leftover vegetables and sprinkling water to keep them fresh.
  • Babuji, Bhaiya, and Chachaji rush to the big vegetable market (mandi) in a tempo at 6:00 am.
  • Setting up the cart before 7:30 am because regular customers go to work early.
  • Perishable vegetables (spinach, tomatoes, bananas) that spoil quickly vs hardy vegetables (potatoes, onions, garlic) that last days.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 Why does Vaishali's father try to sell the previous day's vegetables first? Why does he constantly sprinkle water on vegetables during hot summer afternoons? Livelihood & Food Preservation 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Why previous day's vegetables are sold first:
Unsold vegetables from yesterday lose freshness quickly. If they are not sold early in the morning, they will turn stale, soft, and rotten by noon, causing heavy financial losses to the family.

2. Why water is sprinkled constantly:
In hot dry summer winds (loo), vegetables rapidly lose internal moisture through evaporation, becoming wilted, dry, and unappealing to customers. Sprinkling clean water keeps leafy vegetables, gourds, and tomatoes crisp, fresh, and hydrated.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Financial and perishable reason for selling older stock first 1.5 M
Biological hydration function of water sprinkling in heat 1.5 M
Q2 Why does Vaishali's father wake up at 3 AM every morning? Why does he try to sell previous day's vegetables first? Vegetable Commerce • Mandi to Market 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Waking up at 3 AM:
Vaishali's father and elder brother must reach the wholesale Big Mandi before dawn to purchase the freshest seasonal vegetables directly from arriving farmer trucks at good prices before other retail vendors arrive.

2. Selling Previous Day's Vegetables First:
Older vegetables lose moisture and freshness quickly. If not sold immediately in the morning, they will rot and spoil, causing financial loss to the family. Once old stock is cleared, fresh vegetables fetched from the mandi are displayed.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Early morning mandi procurement explained 1.5 M
Perishability of unsold vegetables explained 1.5 M

Spinach, Potato, Tomato, Onion, Banana, Garlic. Food Storage • Perishable vs. Non-Perishable 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Categorization of Produce:
• (a) Spoil Quickly (High moisture, thin skin): Spinach, Tomato, Banana (must be consumed within 1–2 days).
• (b) Stay Fresh for Many Days (Dry skin, root/bulb tubers): Potato, Onion, Garlic (can be stored in cool dry places for weeks without rotting).
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme

Chapter 16: A Busy Month

Gijubhai Badheka's Letter: Bird Nests, Beak Adaptations, Animal Teeth & Avian Parental Care

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Letter written in April 1936 by pioneering educator Gijubhai Badheka from Bal Mandir, Bhavnagar, Gujarat.
  • Diverse bird nests and architecture:
  • 1. Indian Robin: Lays eggs among roadside stones; nest lined with grass, soft wool, roots, and hair.
  • 2. Crow: Builds messy nests high on trees using twigs and even iron wire.
  • 3. Koel (Cuckoo): Does NOT build a nest; lays eggs slyly in crow's nest; crow hatches them.
  • 4. Tailor Bird: Stitches two broad leaves together with sharp beak; lays eggs in the leafy pouch.
  • 5. Weaver Bird (Baya): Male weaves beautiful hanging bottleneck nests; female inspects all and chooses the best.
  • Bird beaks and animal teeth adaptations (cow, cat, snake, squirrel teeth that never stop growing).
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 How does the Weaver Bird (Baya) choose its mate? Why doesn't the Koel build its own nest? Why do squirrels gnaw continuously on hard objects? Ornithology • Bird Behavior 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Weaver Bird Mate Selection:
The male Weaver Bird weaves intricate, beautiful, hanging woven bottle-shaped nests from tall grass fibers. The female bird inspects every single nest in the tree colony and chooses the one that is strongest, best ventilated, and most secure to lay her eggs.

2. Koel's Nest Parasitism:
The Koel (cuckoo) does not build its own nest. It slyly lays its eggs in an unsuspecting crow's nest. Because the eggs look very similar, the crow faithfully incubates and hatches the Koel's chicks alongside its own.

3. Why Squirrels Gnaw Continuously:
A squirrel's front teeth (incisors) grow continuously throughout its entire life. If a squirrel does not constantly gnaw on hard nuts and wood to grind them down, its teeth will grow so long that it won't be able to close its mouth or eat, leading to death.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Weaver bird male nest building and female inspection 1.5 M
Koel laying eggs in crow's nest (brood parasitism) 1.0 M
Squirrel incisors growing continuously requiring grinding 1.5 M
Q2 Describe how the following birds construct their nests: (a) Indian Robin, (b) Tailorbird, (c) Weaver Bird. Ornithology • Bird Nests 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Nest Construction Styles:
• (a) Indian Robin: Builds soft cup nests in low stone crevices or bush forks using dry grass, roots, animal hair, wool, and soft cotton swabs.
• (b) Tailorbird (दर्जिन चिड़िया): Uses its needle-sharp beak like a sewing needle to pierce and stitch two broad green leaves together with plant fibers, creating a cozy pocket nest.
• (c) Male Weaver Bird (बया): Intricately weaves a beautiful pendant-shaped pouch nest with a hanging entrance tunnel using grass strips. The female inspects all nests and chooses the best one to lay eggs.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Accurate architectural style described for all three birds 3.0 M
Q3 How are the beaks of an Eagle and a Sunbird adapted to their specific food habits? Functional Morphology • Bird Beaks & Claws 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Beak Adaptations:
• Eagle: Has a short, heavy, hooked, razor-sharp beak designed to tear tough meat and flesh of hunted prey (rats, snakes, fish).
• Sunbird: Has a long, slender, curved, straw-like beak perfectly designed to probe deep inside tubular flowers to suck sweet nectar without damaging blossoms.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Hooked meat-tearing beak of eagle vs slender nectar-sucking beak of sunbird 2.0 M

Chapter 17: Nandita in Mumbai

Rural-Urban Contrast, Slum Tenements (Chawls), High-Rise Skyscrapers & Water Woes

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Nandita comes from a village to Mumbai for her mother's hospital treatment.
  • Contrasts in living conditions:
  • 1. Mama's Chawl room: Single room where family sleeps, cooks, sits, and washes; public toilet shared by the whole lane (filthy and foul-smelling).
  • 2. Village House: One room but separate open courtyard, separate cooking area, and separate outdoor bathing space.
  • Water struggles: In the chawl, waking at 4:00 am to fight in long queues at the public street tap. In the high-rise skyscraper (Babita's flat), water flows continuously from shiny taps.
  • Experiencing elevators for the first time; Chowpatty beach and Mumbai sea view.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 What differences did Nandita find between getting water in her village and getting water in Mumbai's chawl? Why was she afraid of taking the high-rise lift initially? Sociological Contrast • Urban Living 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Difference in Water Collection:
• In the Village: There were no water taps, but Nandita walked 20 minutes to a clean village pond or well. There were never any fights or shouting; water was available throughout the day.
• In Mumbai's Chawl: Water arrived at a single public tap only from 4:00 am to 5:00 am. If you didn't reach on time, there was no water for the whole day. People pushed, fought, and screamed in long bucket queues.

2. Fear of the Lift:
Nandita had never seen a multi-story iron cage moving vertically. When she entered the lift with multiple people and the doors slid shut, the sudden upward acceleration made her stomach churn, causing her to hold onto the metal railing in panic.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Detailed contrast between village pond and Mumbai public tap queues 2.0 M
Psychological explanation of first-time lift vertigo and fear 1.0 M
Q2 Compare Nandita's village house with her Mama's house in Mumbai regarding space, cooking, and water supply. Urban Sociology • Chawl Life 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Village House vs. Mumbai Chawl Room:
1. Space: Village house has an open courtyard, separate veranda, and distinct rooms; Mama's chawl is a single cramped room where the family sits, sleeps, and cooks.
2. Cooking: Village house has a separate outdoor cooking chulha; in Mumbai, cooking is done in a corner of the same small room.
3. Water Supply: Village has a pond or well 20 minutes away where water is fetched peacefully; in Mumbai, a public street tap opens at 4 AM for only a short time, leading to fierce shouting and fighting among residents.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three distinct points of contrast (space, cooking, water access) 3.0 M

Nandita's Experience in the High-Rise:
Nandita was amazed to see an elevator (lift) that zoomed up like a big flying iron cage with lights and fans. Inside Babloo's flat on the 12th floor, she was stunned to see separate rooms for sitting, sleeping, and dining, and a bathroom with running taps where water flowed continuously while people let it run wastefully.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Lift experience and amazement at indoor plumbing contrast 2.0 M

Analytical Task: Why did this upset Nandita, and what should every citizen do to prevent water wastage?

Nandita was heartbroken because she knew how desperately her Mama and aunties fought at 4:00 am for just a single bucket of water, while here precious drinking water was poured down the drain carelessly. Chapter 18: Too Much Water, Too Little Water

Water Crises: Water Parks in Maharashtra, Diarrhea in Nalgonda & Village Water Committees (Holgundi)

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The paradox of water distribution: Massive water parks wasting millions of litres on joy slides in Bazar Gaon, Maharashtra, while neighboring farmers suffer severe drinking water shortages.
  • Waterborne diseases: Drinking contaminated water causing severe diarrhea and vomiting.
  • Life-saving home remedy: Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) — 1 teaspoon sugar + a pinch of salt dissolved in 1 glass of boiled, cooled water.
  • Empowerment: Children's Water Panchayat (Bheema Sangh) in Holgundi, Karnataka, rejuvenating dried village stepwells and restoring water security.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 What causes severe dehydration during diarrhea and vomiting? How do you prepare a homemade Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) step-by-step? Public Health & First Aid Science 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Cause of Dehydration:
During severe diarrhea and vomiting, the body rapidly loses critical water and essential mineral salts (electrolytes). If these fluids are not replaced immediately, vital organs can fail, which is especially fatal for young children.

2. Preparation of Homemade ORS:
• Step 1: Boil one glass of clean drinking water and let it cool completely.
• Step 2: Add one level teaspoon of sugar (provides instant energy and aids electrolyte absorption).
• Step 3: Add one small pinch of salt (restores sodium electrolytes; taste should not be saltier than tears).
• Step 4: Stir thoroughly until completely dissolved. Sip slowly throughout the day.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Biological danger of water and electrolyte loss 1.0 M
Exact 4-step preparation recipe (boiled water, 1 tsp sugar, pinch salt) 2.0 M
Q2 What causes diarrhea and vomiting? How can you prepare an Oral Rehydration Solution (ORS) at home in an emergency? Public Health • Waterborne Illness & ORS 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Causes of Diarrhea and Vomiting:
Drinking water contaminated with sewage bacteria, amoebae, or eating unwashed, fly-infested food causes intestinal infections, leading to rapid loss of body water and vital salts (dehydration).

2. Home-Made ORS Preparation:
• Boil one glass (approx. 250 ml) of clean drinking water and let it cool.
• Add one level teaspoon of sugar and a tiny pinch of salt.
• Stir until completely dissolved. Sip slowly to replenish lost fluids and electrolytes.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Contaminated water/food etiology explained 1.5 M
Accurate water, sugar, and salt proportions for home ORS 1.5 M
Q3 In the chapter, a luxurious water park operated with splashing fountains while neighbouring villagers had no drinking water. What moral lesson does this highlight? Civic Equity • Water Commercialization 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Lesson on Water Justice:
Water is a fundamental human right essential for survival. Wasting millions of litres of precious potable water on recreational slides and water fountains while neighboring poor citizens queue for hours for a single bucket of dirty water represents gross civic inequality. Clean drinking water for survival must always take priority over commercial entertainment.

🌟 NEP 2020 Competency-Based Case Study (CBQ)

Bheema Sangh (Children's Water Panchayat)

Real-World Environment Context: In Holgundi village (Karnataka), adults gave up farming because village wells had dried up. The children's panchayat (Bheema Sangh) took charge.

Analytical Task: How did the children of Bheema Sangh restore water security to their village?

The children surveyed the hill slopes and discovered the ancient community tank was choked with mud, weeds, and cracked walls. They convinced elders, cleaned the silt, repaired stone bunds, and planted trees on the slopes. When monsoon rains arrived, the tank held water, recharging underground wells so farming resumed.
CBSE Assessment Rubric: 1.5 Marks for identifying choked tank and desilting; 1.5 Marks for bund repair and groundwater recharge.

Chapter 19: Abdul in the Garden

Plant Roots: Taproot vs Fibrous Roots, Desert Oak (Australia) & Banyan Aerial Roots

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • The vital functions of roots: Absorbing water and mineral salts, anchoring plants firmly against stormy winds.
  • Roots we eat as vegetables: Carrot (gajar), radish (mooli), beetroot (chukandar), sweet potato (shakarkand).
  • Desert Oak (Australia): A desert tree with roots that go 30 times deeper than its height underground until they reach the water table. Local people use thin straws to drink water from its trunk during droughts.
  • Banyan Tree: Pillar-like hanging aerial roots that grow downward from branches into the ground to provide massive structural support.
  • Laws protecting trees: Needing official government permission to prune or fell roadside trees.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 What are the unique characteristics of the Desert Oak tree found in Australia? Why was Abdul surprised when he tried to pull out a small grass plant from the garden bed? Plant Physiology & Adaptations 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Desert Oak Tree (Australia):
• Grows as tall as a classroom wall, but has very few leaves.
• Its roots drill downward into the desert soil almost 30 times deeper than its height until they touch the subterranean water table.
• Water is stored directly inside the tree trunk. During droughts, indigenous people insert thin hollow pipes into the trunk to drink clean water.

2. Why Abdul was surprised by grass roots:
Abdul thought pulling out a tiny grass blade would be effortless. But when he tugged, the grass didn't budge—instead, he broke the pea plant stalk! He was amazed to discover that tiny grass plants have extensive, tough fibrous root networks spreading deep into the soil, anchoring the ground firmly.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Three facts about Australian Desert Oak (deep roots, water in trunk) 2.5 M
Explanation of grass fibrous roots anchorage power 1.5 M
Q2 Why was Abdul unable to pull out a small clump of grass easily, even though he could break a pea climber stem effortlessly? Plant Anatomy • Root Systems 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Strength of Grass Roots:
Although grass leaves look delicate, its roots are fibrous, dense, and deeply entwined with surrounding soil particles. Roots act like strong anchors, holding tightly to the earth to resist heavy rains and strong winds. In contrast, the stem of a pea plant is soft, thin, and green, making it easy to snap.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Fibrous root anchoring mechanism explained 1.5 M
Contrast with tender aerial climbing stem 1.5 M
Q3 What is the Desert Oak tree? How do its roots survive in the arid Australian outback? Ecological Adaptations • The Desert Oak 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
The Desert Oak Tree:
The Desert Oak is a native tree found in the dry deserts of Australia. It has very few leaves to minimize water loss through transpiration. Its roots grow straight down into the soil up to 30 times deeper than the height of the tree until they reach deep subterranean water tables. Local indigenous people insert thin pipes into tree trunks during severe droughts to drink stored water.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Australian habitat and leaf adaptation 1.5 M
Extreme root depth (30x tree height) reaching groundwater 1.5 M

Chapter 20: Eating Together

Community Feasting: Bihu Festival in Assam, Bhela Ghar & The Mid-Day Meal Scheme

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Class parties and community celebrations: Joy of sharing food without discrimination.
  • Magh Bihu festival in Assam: Celebrated on 14th and 15th January (1st and 2nd Magh).
  • Bhela Ghar: Temporary pavilion constructed with bamboo and thatch where the community spends Uruka night feasting.
  • Traditional Bihu cuisine: Bora and Chheva rice (sticky rice boiled in bamboo tubes), fish curry, pitha, and coconut ladoos.
  • The Mid-Day Meal (PM POSHAN) Scheme: Legal right of every primary school student to receive fresh, hot, nutritious food; bridges social caste barriers.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is 'Bhela Ghar', and when is it set on fire during the Bihu festival? What is the supreme objective of the Mid-Day Meal scheme in Indian schools? Festival Traditions & Welfare Programs 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Bhela Ghar & Meji during Bihu:
In Assam, on the eve of Magh Bihu (called Uruka), the entire village constructs a temporary hut out of bamboo, thatch, and straw called Bhela Ghar. Everyone eats a grand feast together inside it at night. Early next morning, after prayers, the Bhela Ghar and Meji (high bonfire) are lit to seek the blessings of Agni (the Fire God) for a rich agricultural harvest.

2. Objective of the Mid-Day Meal Scheme:
By supreme court directive, every primary school student has the fundamental right to hot, freshly cooked, nutritious lunch. It accomplishes two vital goals: (a) Eliminates classroom hunger so poor children can concentrate on studies, and (b) Children of all religions and castes sit in a single row eating together, dismantling caste prejudices.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Detailed explanation of Bhela Ghar, Uruka, and Meji bonfire 2.0 M
Dual goals of Mid-Day Meal (nutrition and social equality) 2.0 M
Q2 Describe the Magh Bihu festival of Assam. What are 'Uruka', 'Bhela Ghar', and 'Meji'? Cultural Festivals • Magh Bihu of Assam 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Magh Bihu:
Magh Bihu is the joyful harvest festival celebrated in Assam in mid-January, marking the end of the winter paddy harvesting season.

2. Key Traditions:
• Uruka: The eve of Bihu where the entire village gathers to cook and feast on fish curry, bora rice, and pitha under the stars.
• Bhela Ghar: A temporary community pavilion constructed in open fields using harvested thatch, bamboo, and dry leaves.
• Meji: A tall conical bonfire of wood and bamboo lit at sunrise on Bihu morning; villagers pray for blessings and offer coconuts and sesame cakes to the sacred fire.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Bihu definition as harvest celebration 1.0 M
Accurate description of Uruka, Bhela Ghar, and Meji 3.0 M
Q3 What is the Mid-Day Meal scheme in government schools? State two major social benefits of this program. Social Welfare • The Mid-Day Meal Scheme 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. Mid-Day Meal Scheme:
A landmark government welfare program under which every child studying in elementary government and government-aided schools is provided with a free, freshly-cooked, nutritious hot lunch every school day.

2. Two Social Benefits:
• Combats Child Malnutrition: Guarantees that poor and undernourished children receive balanced calories and proteins, boosting concentration.
• Promotes Social Equality: Children from all castes, religions, and economic backgrounds sit together side-by-side to eat, eradicating social prejudices.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Program definition and hot meal provision 1.5 M
Two benefits: malnutrition reduction and caste equality 1.5 M

Chapter 21: Food and Fun

Boarding School Life, The Gurudwara Kitchen (Langar) & Selfless Service (Seva)

Environmental Themes, Concepts & Field Observations
  • Boarding school experiences: Living in hostels, missing home food, but enjoying sharing large tiffin boxes with hostel friends.
  • The holy Gurudwara visit: Covering heads with scarves, washing feet, paying respects to the Guru Granth Sahib.
  • The massive community kitchen (Langar): Giant cauldrons of chana-urad dal, vegetable kaddhu, stacks of hot chapatis, and sweet Kada Prasad (semolina halwa cooked in pure desi ghee).
  • The spirit of 'Seva' (Selfless Service): Rich and poor sit side-by-side on floor mats (pangat); volunteers happily roll rotis, serve food, wash metal plates, and sweep floors.
📖 NCERT Textbook Exercise Solutions & Step-by-Step Working (13 Solved Questions)
Q1 What is a 'Langar' in a Gurudwara? How is Kada Prasad prepared, and what values of Seva does a Gurudwara kitchen demonstrate? Community Service & Spiritual Traditions 4 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. What is Langar:
A Langar is a free, sanctified community kitchen maintained by every Sikh Gurudwara worldwide, where hot, wholesome vegetarian food is served round-the-clock to all visitors without any distinction of religion, caste, gender, or wealth.

2. Preparation of Kada Prasad:
Kada Prasad is a sacred halwa prepared in huge iron cauldrons (kadhai) by roasting wheat flour (atta) thoroughly in generous amounts of pure desi ghee until golden brown, then adding sugar and boiling water while stirring vigorously until it turns fragrant, glossy, and smooth.

3. Values of Seva:
Volunteers perform all tasks voluntarily with joyful devotion: cutting vegetables, rolling rotis on hot tavas, serving with folded hands, washing thousands of stainless steel plates, and cleaning the hall. It teaches humility, dignity of labor, and selfless service.
CBSE Step-by-Step Marking Scheme
Definition of Langar and universal equality 1.5 M
Recipe and preparation of Kada Prasad 1.0 M
Values of Seva (humility, selfless community labor) 1.5 M
Q2 What is a 'Langar' in a Gurudwara? How does community service (Seva) foster equality among people? Community Service • Gurudwara Langar 3 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
1. The Langar Tradition:
Langar is a sacred community kitchen in a Sikh Gurudwara where free, hot vegetarian meals (dal, vegetables, rotis, rice, and kheer) are served to all visitors without any discrimination based on religion, caste, gender, or wealth.

2. The Spirit of Seva:
All food is cooked and served voluntarily by devotees (Seva). People roll rotis, stir large cooking cauldrons, wash dishes, and sit together on floor mats (Pangat) in long rows, demonstrating that all human beings are equal in the eyes of God.

Q3 What is 'Karah Parshad', and how is it prepared in large cauldrons at the Gurudwara? Sacred Food • Karah Parshad 2 Marks
✅ Step-by-Step Model Answer & Solution:
Karah Parshad:
Karah Parshad is a sacred halwa blessed and distributed in Gurudwaras. It is prepared in large iron cauldrons by roasting coarse whole-wheat flour (atta) in equal proportions of pure desi ghee until golden brown and aromatic. Boiling water sweetened with equal sugar is then added, stirring vigorously until a rich, smooth, fragrant pudding forms.
